Protesters are demanding development, jobs and dignity, the same slogans that drove the 2011 revolution

Originally published on Global Voices

Screenshot from video ‘Tunisians protest against the president: Critical infrastructure struggling to cope in summer’ on the Al Jazeera English channel on YouTube. Fair use.

This article, by Basma Barakat, was originally published in The New Arab on September 18, 2026. This edited version is republished on Global Voices as part of a content partnership agreement. It is also part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” You can support this coverage by donating here.

Several Tunisian provinces are witnessing growing popular protests demanding development, jobs and dignity, the same slogans that drove the revolution that erupted on January 14, 2011.

For the first time since then, the general public are joining unemployed people in protesting, frustrated after years of unfulfilled promises, unenforced laws and deteriorating conditions.

title: Peter Obi and the Obidient Movement: Nigeria’s Future
content:
By Kester Kenn Klomegah

MOSCOW | 22 September 2026 (IDN) — As the Federal Republic of Nigeria prepares for the 2027 presidential election, the Obidient Movement is seeking to build on the political momentum it generated around Peter Obi’s 2023 candidacy.

The movement attracted significant support among younger Nigerians and sections of the country’s professional and diaspora communities. Its supporters have sought to present it as an alternative to Nigeria’s established political parties, emphasising accountability, economic management, and a different approach to governance.

In this interview, Professor Maurice Okoli, an economist and research fellow associated with the Russian Academy of Sciences, including the Institute for African Studies and IMEMO, and an expert with the Valdai Discussion Club, discusses his involvement in the movement, its international outreach and what he believes it must do differently before the 2027 election.

title: TPS ja Ihmisoikeusliitto: Ihmisoikeudet kuuluvat urheilun ytimeen
content:
Lauantaina 3.10. pelattavan TPS–JYP-ottelun yhteydessä nostetaan esiin Ihmisoikeusliiton Älä riko urheilua -kampanjaa.

Turussa pelataan lauantaina 3.10. TPS:n ja Ihmisoikeusliiton yhteinen teemaottelu, kun TPS kohtaa Gatorade Centerissä JYPin. Yhdenvertaisuusottelussa nostetaan esiin Ihmisoikeusliiton Älä riko urheilua -työtä ja sen ydinviestiä: Ihmisoikeudet kuuluvat urheilun ytimeen. TPS ja Ihmisoikeusliitto haluavat yhdessä olla rakentamassa urheilumaailmaa, jossa jokainen voi urheilla turvallisesti ja omana itsenään. Kampanjan viestit näkyvät laajasti ottelutapahtumassa. Ihmisoikeudet eivät vielä toteudu urheilussa kaikille. Haasteita on niin rakenteissa, toimintatavoissa kuin arjen tilanteissakin, eikä jääkiekko ole tästä poikkeus. Älä riko urheilua -kampanjan sanoin: Urheilu on rikki, jos lapsen oikeuksia ei turvata, jos rasismiin ei puututa järjestelmällisesti, jos sukupuolten tasa-arvo ei toteudu, jos seksuaali- ja sukupuolivähemmistöt eivät voi urheilla omana itsenään tai jos vammaisilla ihmisillä ei ole yhdenvertaista mahdollisuutta urheilla.

title: Why investigative teams fall into conflict — and what to do about it
content:
A room full of investigative journalists closed their eyes, took a sheet of A4 paper and followed a set of instructions. Fold it in half. Tear off the upper right corner. Fold it again. Tear off the lower right corner. No questions were allowed.

When they opened their eyes and unfolded the paper, the results were markedly different. Some had intricate patterns. Others were little more than shredded paper.

For Emma Thomasson, who was leading a workshop on communication and conflict at IJ4EU’s UNCOVERED Conference in Budapest, the exercise illustrated a basic problem in collaborative work: giving people the same instructions does not mean they will understand them in the same way.

“The point here is that communication is difficult, and particularly difficult if we are not all from the same background,” said Thomasson, a former Reuters bureau chief who now offers training and consulting on leadership, communication, innovation and workplace wellbeing.

content:
The Nordic Film Club is dedicating its October edition to Finnish cinema with the film Girl Picture (2022), directed by Alli Haapasalo. Reflecting the themes of the film, this screening is being organized as part of the International Day of the Girl, in collaboration with the Embassy of Finland, which is taking part in the Girls Takeover campaign. Girls Takeover is a global initiative led by Plan International, in which young girls take on high-level leadership positions for a day. On this occasion, a young girl will be welcomed as an “ambassador for a day.”

Girl Picture follows three young women, Mimmi, Rönkkö and Emma, on the threshold of adulthood. Best friends Mimmi and Rönkkö support each other unconditionally and dream of a life full of adventure, experiences and passion. Emma, meanwhile, has devoted her life to figure skating and achievement. When their paths cross, new possibilities open up for them. Between first loves, desire, pleasure, friendship and the search for self-discovery, their lives take unexpected turns. Three Fridays are enough to turn their world upside down.

title: Meeting with Commissioner for Startups, Research and Innovation Ekaterina Zaharieva
content:
Last week, COMMUNIA joined IFLA, LIBER and SPARC Europe for a meeting with Ekaterina Zaharieva, Commissioner for Startups, Research and Innovation, to discuss the upcoming European Research Area (ERA) Act.

During this constructive exchange, we highlighted two priorities: an EU-wide secondary publication right to make publicly funded research openly available, and a general scientific research exception to create a harmonised copyright framework that enables researchers across Europe to use and build on copyright-protected research materials.

As we have argued  since the beginning of this mandate, Europe must remove persistent barriers that prevent libraries and other knowledge institutions from fulfilling their public mission, particularly in the digital environment. The ERA Act offers an important opportunity to address these barriers and help turn the “Fifth Freedom”—the free movement of researchers, knowledge and technology across the EU—into a reality.

We thank Commissioner Zaharieva and her cabinet for welcoming us and engaging with our proposals. We look forward to the Commission’s proposal for the ERA Act and to continuing this dialogue as the legislation takes shape.

title: The New Influence Machine
content:
A slew of recent reporting has looked at how a new generation of lobbyists is emerging to shape the Trump administration’s views, change their policies or advocate for causes. These figures are not traditional lobbyists, but people with influence over and access to key members of the Trump administration, often extending all the way to the White House and Trump family. Last week, Anne Applebaum described in The Atlantic, how “informal envoys, private companies, online grifters, and hardened ideologues both inside and outside the government matter more,” than traditional ways of lobbying, diplomacy and policy making. CBS News investigated and interviewed pardon brokers, who charge hundreds of thousands of dollars to petition the White House for clemency, going around the Department of Justice. They justified their fees with costs including fundraising dinners and trips to Mar-a-Lago. Politico Influence reported that a Gen-Z online content creator is conducting influence operations for an Israeli defence company, in at least his second foreign lobbying contract. 

Curious how this reporting aligned with larger patterns and areas of concern, ACDC revisited some of the data analysis for our July report into foreign lobbying for high-risk individuals. In that report, we found a thriving and lucrative “leniency lobby” that seeks to secure U.S. political support, pardons and sanctions relief for individuals from around the world who have been implicated in corruption, human rights abuses and other offenses.

title: Kirjasto puntarissa
content:
Kirjastolaki ei määrittele tarkasti, kuinka paljon henkilöstöä kirjastossa pitäisi olla tai kuinka suuret tilat tarvitaan. Siksi kirjastojen on tärkeää osoittaa palvelujensa laatu ja riittävyys itsearvioinnin avulla.

Aiempi kirjastolaki antoi nykyistä tarkempia lähtökohtia kirjastopalvelujen järjestämiseen. Opetus- ja kulttuuriministeriö saattoi esimerkiksi antaa suosituksia henkilöstön määrästä ja kirjaston pinta-alasta, joihin kirjastot pystyivät vetoamaan hakiessaan lisäresursseja.

Kymmenen vuotta sitten voimaan tullut nykyinen kirjastolaki jättää enemmän harkintavaltaa kunnille ja kirjastoille. Samalla vastuu palvelujen kehittämisestä ja niiden laadun osoittamisesta on siirtynyt entistä vahvemmin kirjastoille itselleen.

Siksi kirjastojen työn keskeinen väline on itsearviointi, johon myös kirjastolaki velvoittaa. Sen avulla kirjasto voi arvioida, vastaavatko palvelut kuntalaisten tarpeita ja toteutuvatko lain tavoitteet käytännössä.

”Laki ei määrittele palveluille vähimmäistasoa, vaan palvelun taso määrittyy itsearvioinnin kautta”, sanoo Lupa- ja valvontaviraston kirjastotoimen ylitarkastaja Virpi Launonen.

title: 11 Rekisteröidyn oikeuksien toteuttamisesta kieltäytyminen ja muutoksenhaku
content:
Rekisteröidyn oikeuksien toteuttaminen on lähtökohta. Rekisterinpitäjä saa rajoittaa tai olla toteuttamatta rekisteröidyn oikeutta vain, jos rajoittamiselle on nimenomainen oikeudellinen peruste tietosuoja-asetuksessa, tietosuojalaissa tai muussa sovellettavassa lainsäädännössä tai jos oikeuden toteuttamisen edellytykset eivät täyty, esimerkiksi jos rekisteröidyn henkilöllisyyttä ei pystytä luotettavasti varmistamaan. Pelkkä pyynnön toteuttamisesta aiheutuva työmäärä, kustannus tai muu organisatorinen rasite ei oikeuta kieltäytymään pyynnön käsittelystä.

Jos rekisterinpitäjä kieltäytyy toteuttamasta pyynnön kokonaan tai osittain, sen on annettava rekisteröidylle perusteltu vastaus ilman aiheetonta viivytystä ja viimeistään kuukauden kuluessa pyynnön vastaanottamisesta. Samalla rekisteröidylle on ilmoitettava käytettävissä olevista oikeussuojakeinoista. Esimerkkivastaus löytyy tämän ohjeen liitteestä 4.

For any country with an FOI regime, oversight is vital — otherwise, there’s nowhere for people to turn when the system fails.

In the UK we have the ICO, the Information Commissioner's Office; and there are regulatory authorities in many different forms in countries around the world.

But what do regulators do? And what are they able they do? In this free webinar, we hear from representatives of both the UK and Chile's overseers.

We hope you'll join us on Sept 28: find out more and book here.

Christian is Head of the Training and Promotion Unit at Consejo para la Transparencia (Council of Transparency), Chile’s equivalent of the ICO.

Aiden, from the UK's Information Commissioner’s Office, is Senior Upstream Regulation Officer in their FOI and Transparency division.

title: Why China Will Rule AI
content:
In his 2013 book, “The End of Power,” Moisés Naim famously wrote that “power no longer buys as much as it did in the past. In the twenty-first century, power is easier to get, harder to use—and easier to lose.”

That may be true for deconstructed authority in the West, but it is not true in China where the weighty center of authority remains in the un-deconstructed Communist Party. There, power is hard for others to get, easily used and nearly impossible ever to lose.

This systemic incapacity of open societies puts them at a disadvantage when it comes to ruling frontier AI models.

Endless appeals about the dangers of unleashed AI from rosters of the most eminent scientists, Papal encyclicals and monarchical meditations gain no effective traction. The public is warily confused and feels helpless to affect the set course of events. By and large, legislators appear hopelessly clueless and slow on the draw as AI development exponentially accelerates.

title: Albanian Court Orders House Arrest for Intelligence Chief
content:
An Albanian court has ordered the director of the State Intelligence Service (SHISH), Vlora Hyseni, to be put under house arrest and suspended from public duty as part of a sweeping investigation into public tender fraud, the Special Prosecutor’s Office (SPAK) announced Tuesday. The development prompted Prime Minister Edi Rama to announce her immediate removal from office.

The Special Court against Corruption and Organized Crime (GJKKO) approved the security measures at the request of SPAK. Prosecutors are investigating Hyseni for allegedly assisting a perpetrator of a criminal offense and disclosing state secrets.

However, the house arrest order could not be immediately executed because Hyseni was in Baku, Azerbaijan, attending an international conference of intelligence service heads when officers searched her apartment.

Speaking from New York, Prime Minister Edi Rama said Hyseni’s dismissal is immediate and that he will consult President Bajram Begaj to appoint a successor, emphasizing that the court must determine her guilt or innocence independently.

title: How Alan Turing and His Fellow Codebreakers Broke the Nazis’ “Unbreakable” Enigma Code
content:
There was a time when you could just go out and buy an Enigma machine. In the early nineteen-twenties, any organization with a need to keep its communications secret could order a few of those brand-new devices from Germany and rest assured that any messages encoded using them would be safe from prying eyes. It didn’t take long for the military to catch on to the Enigma’s usefulness. Just a few years after the machine came on the market, it had been adopted by the German Navy, Army, and Air Force, and made possible the rapid, secret coordination central to the technique we now call blitzkrieg. When World War II began, Axis forces were confident, as anyone in possession of an unbreakable code might well be.

As history played out, of course, that code turned out to be breakable. That this came as a surprise to the Nazis makes sense if you watch the new video above from Veritasium, which opens up an actual Enigma machine and explains its inner workings. Each letter typed into its keyboard passes through a series of interchangeable rotors wired together, then comes back through in the opposite direction, resulting in a particular substitute letter.

title: The FBI Anti-Corruption Squad Was Circling Susan Collins — Until Trump Got in the Way
content:
In the final weeks of 2019, a top fundraiser for Sen. Susan Collins walked into a perilous meeting at a Corner Bakery in Washington, D.C.

For the first time in her two-decade Senate career, the Republican lawmaker from Maine was in danger of losing her seat. President Donald Trump’s dismal approval ratings were dragging her down in the polls, and she was falling behind her likely 2020 Democratic challenger in fundraising.

Scott Reed, head of the Collins super PAC, was on a mission to close that gap. Reed was meeting that day with three executives from a Hawaiian defense contractor, Navatek. A year earlier, Collins had helped their company land a multimillion-dollar Navy research contract in Maine. Now, seated at a coffee shop not far from the U.S. Capitol, Reed asked them for a $500,000 donation.

Government contractors are banned from making political contributions. More consequentially, for the company to offer donations to Collins in exchange for an official action, or for Collins to accept, would constitute criminal bribery.

title: Sissejuhataja: õigus olla see, kes oled
content:
Hannele Valkeeniemi kirjutis valmis sissejuhatajaks septembrikuu uudiskirjale.

Kultuur on kunst ja teadus, kontserdid ja teatrietendused, kultuuripärand… Võib ka öelda lühemalt, et kultuur on meie olemise viis. Teisisõnu, kultuur ütleb, kes me oleme, millised on meie väärtused ja kombed kohtudes teistega. Aga mis siis, kui meil ei lasta olla need, kes me oleme? Väikesed rahvad, kellel pole oma riiki ega muid iseolemise tunnuseid, saavad olla olemas ainult tänu oma kultuurile. Kui ka see kaob, ei jää järele midagi peale tühja kesta. title: New Research Paper on Federal AI-CSAM Prosecutions
content:
Together with Cyndie Demeocq at U of Edinburgh, today I’m releasing a paper analyzing 71 federal criminal cases, filed around the US from 2022-2025, that somehow involve AI-generated or -morphed CSAM or child obscenity. It's available on SSRN here.

We’re also releasing the dataset of cases (with an appendix of 2026 cases) on GitHub. Our hope is that this data will be useful to others. I believe this is the largest public collection of federal AI-CSAM cases to date (though I assume there’s an internal list at DOJ).

Our top-line finding: existing laws are working just fine in AI-CSAM prosecutions, at least in the cases prosecutors chose to bring. (We can’t know what cases they decided not to bring, or why.) Most defendants pled guilty (as usual); the few who went to trial all got convicted. Prison sentences are longer than average for CSAM or obscenity cases. Out of 71 cases studied, only half a dozen are still pending.

title: Saatko olla se, joka olet
content:

Kulttuuri on taidetta ja tiedettä, tapahtumia, kultturiperintöä – mutta viime kädessä se on tapamme olla olemassa. Eli kulttuuri kertoo, keitä me olemme, mitkä ovat arvomme ja tapamme kohdata toiset. title: Ny bok utforskar pepparkakans rika och kryddstarka historia
content:
Hur blev ett exklusivt medeltida läkemedel en av Nordens mest älskade kakor? I den nya boken Pepparkakor. En kryddig historia berättar mat- och måltidsforskaren Yrsa Lindqvist historien om bakverket som färdats genom århundraden, kontinenter och kulturer.

 En doft av kanel, nejlika och kardemumma väcker minnen till liv, och få kan tänka sig att fira jul utan knapriga, väldoftande pepparkakor. Som en självklar del av julfirandet förenar kakan tradition och kreativitet – samtidigt som den bär på en komplex historia.

– I pepparkakan möts vardag och högtid, medicin och njutning, vilket gör den till ett bakverk med ovanligt många lager, en smak som bär på minnen, omsorg och fest, säger Yrsa Lindqvist.

I Pepparkakor följer Lindqvist kakans resa från det forna Egypten till dagens julbord. Under medeltiden såldes pepparkakor som läkemedel och ansågs kunna lindra allt från magbesvär till melankoli, och först långt senare blev de ett sött bakverk för en bred publik. Samtidigt speglar pepparkakans historia en större berättelse om kryddhandel, medicin, globalisering och koloniala erövringar.

title: Cybercriminal group claims to steal thousands of FBI employee records
content:
The FBI said it is investigating a possible breach into its online jobs portal, after a prolific cybercrime group publicly claimed to have stolen personal information of FBI personnel.

“The FBI is aware of claims regarding unauthorized activity affecting FBIjobs.gov and is currently investigating,” the FBI National Press Office said in a statement.

Confirmation of an ongoing investigation came hours after a cybercriminal group known as ShinyHunters posted a message online claiming it had stolen “very sensitive” data on “almost all” FBI agents, as well as those who had applied for jobs at the bureau.

The group provided a sample of stolen data affecting 5,000 supposed FBI agents to 404 Media, which first reported on the alleged hack. The sample data set included agent names, home addresses, phone numbers and information on agents’ spouses, the outlet said.

title: As Ukraine rebuilds amid constant Russian attacks, small towns and villages are being sidelined
content:
In the early days of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Russian armoured columns pushed east along the Zhytomyr highway towards Kyiv. Makariv, a small settlement of about 10,000 people 36 miles west of Kyiv, sat on their route. The town was wrecked in the month of fighting that ensued.

Roughly 40% of the settlement’s infrastructure was destroyed and the bodies of 132 executed civilians were recovered by April 2022. A 2026 account puts the total death toll as high as 238. Yet Makariv was never taken. It held, with Russian forces only taking control of about 10% of its land, and Kyiv held behind it.

“For some reason, Makariv was bypassed in the press,” said local museum curator Vitaly Gedz in a 2026 interview. “They wrote about Makariv twice, ‘it was occupied and then liberated’ … It was only 10% occupied, but it was very badly destroyed.”

On a visit to Makariv the previous year, we visited Gedz’s museum. Among the objects on display there were military maps recovered after Russian forces withdrew. Russian units were found to be carrying Soviet-era sheets, some of which dated back to 1969, with the modern border between Russia and Ukraine often added in pen.

title: Russia-Ukraine war is accelerating the dangerous race toward fully autonomous drones
content:
A battlefield dominated by fully autonomous drones capable of selecting and engaging targets without human intervention sounds like a dystopian sci-fi plot. And while that scenario has not yet arrived, the conflict between Russia and Ukraine has moved modern warfare a notch down that road.

In recent years, both nations have deployed semi-autonomous drones in combat and are rapidly racing toward fully autonomous unmanned aerial vehicles.

Given these developments and the pace of Russian and Ukrainian drone production, a battlefield with hundreds to thousands of fully autonomous drones operating is plausible within the next few years. Yet, the technology underpinning autonomous warfare risks outpacing the Russian and Ukrainian frameworks for maintaining some degree of human control over weapons.

As an expert on weapons technology, I worry that the battlefield incentives to deploy more autonomous drones will completely push aside human targeting decisions related to using proportional force, avoiding strikes on non-combatants and limiting collateral damage.

title: Public Data, AI, and the Future of the Catalog
content:
The following is taken from remarks delivered on the “AI and Government Data” panel at the AI for Library, Archives, and Museums 2026 conference.

I begin by addressing how we might define public data. It is, in short, data whose value is not determined by the marketplace, by its commodification, or by what Marx would call its “use value.” Public data may function in all of these ways, but its value is defined by something more abstract and less quantifiable. It serves civil society, and without it, an intrinsic public good—the health and safety of a polity, the protection of an environment, the advancement of creative and critical thinking—would be lost.

As stewards of the past and curators of the present who work in service of the future, we in libraries, archives, and museums have long turned our attention to cultural heritage—both in its material and digital forms—for their value as public goods. In the United States, we have, since the first Census in 1790, more or less “Render[ed] therefore unto Caesar” the production and dissemination of information produced by the government for the governed.

title: Finnish Photonics Hub Joensuu Opens New International Test Program for Experts
content:
The City of Joensuu, one of Europe’s leading photonics hubs, has launched Test Joensuu, a new international residency-style program designed for a photonics professional, researcher, entrepreneur, or light artist seeking to develop an idea, project, product or collaboration within a world-class photonics ecosystem.

Applications for the program are open from September 21 to October 4, 2026. One participant will be selected for a visit to Joensuu, Finland, from November 20 to 29, 2026. The City of Joensuu will cover the travel and accommodation costs.

Unlike traditional international promotion efforts that take expertise abroad, Test Joensuu brings global talent directly into the innovation environment where research, education, technology companies, and creative industries work side by side.

“Joensuu is internationally recognized for its strong photonics expertise, but we are continuously looking for new ways to showcase our capabilities. Test Joensuu creates genuine opportunities for interaction between researchers, companies, students, and international experts,” says Markku Pyykkönen, Marketing Director of the City of Joensuu.

title: Varustelu kasvattaa ilmastolaskua – armeijoiden päästöt jäävät yhä piiloon
content:
Johanna Kohvakka

Kun listataan maailman suurimpia kasvihuonekaasupäästäjiä, asevoimat jäävät yleensä luetteloiden ulkopuolelle.

Se ei tarkoita, että niiden ilmastovaikutus olisi pieni. Ongelma on pikemminkin siinä, ettei yhtä, kattavaa lukua ole helppo muodostaa, sillä sotilaallisia päästöjä lasketaan ja raportoidaan hajanaisesti.

Yhdysvaltain armeijan, Pentagonin, sotilasoperaatioiden ja tukikohtien kasvihuonekaasupäästöjen on arvioitu olleen vuonna 2023 noin 48 miljoonaa tonnia hiilidioksidiekvivalenttia. Se on enemmän kuin esimerkiksi koko Suomen samana vuonna tuottamat kasvihuonekaasupäästöt ilman maankäyttösektoria, jotka olivat 41 miljoonaa tonnia.

Vertailu ei ole aivan yksi yhteen, sillä kansallisten päästöinventaarioiden ja Pentagonin päästölaskennan rajaukset poikkeavat toisistaan. Se kertoo silti mittakaavasta: yhden valtion puolustushallinnon toiminnan ilmastovaikutus vastaa keskikokoisen teollisuusmaan vuotuisia päästöjä.

Yhdysvaltain armeijaa määritelläänkin usein maailman instituutioiden suurimmaksi kasvihuonekaasupäästäjäksi. Tutkimuksissa sen vuotuisten päästöjen on todettu ylittävän yli sadan valtion päästöt erikseen tarkasteltuina.

title: WITNESS releases report on five lessons from the Nepal floods for verifying what’s real
content:
WITNESS has released a new report examining five lessons from the Nepal floods for verifying what’s real in the age of AI. Drawing on cases investigated by fact-checkers and on WITNESS’ work, the report examines the limits of AI detection, the growing role of technology companies in determining what is real, and why human investigation remains essential in a crisis.

On 26 August, a glacial collapse high on the Nepal-Tibet border sent a wall of ice, rock and water down the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli valleys. More than 1,380 people were killed in Nepal and over 5,100 remained missing. Within hours, social media filled with footage of the disaster. Some of it was real, but much of it was not. Fact-checkers identified AI-generated videos, footage recycled from other disasters, and authentic footage that was mistakenly questioned as AI-generated. Some fake videos also disputed the cause of the disaster, attributing the floods to a Chinese-built dam or a missile strike rather than the documented glacial collapse.

title: Pehmeät asiat ovat kovimpia kilpailutekijöitä
content:
Minna Mattila-Aalto

Mitä tapahtuu, kun organisaatio haluaa parantaa tuottavuuttaan? Se alkaa mitata enemmän. Entä jos juuri siksi tuottavuus ei kasva?

Havaintojeni mukaan organisaatiot alkavat mitata yhä enemmän suoritteita, käyttöastetta, läpimenoaikoja, kustannuksia ja tehokkuutta. Mittaaminen tuntuu turvalliselta, sillä luvut näyttävät objektiivisilta. Niiden avulla voidaan vertailla, ohjata ja tehdä päätöksiä.

Entä jos kaikkein tärkein jääkin mittaamatta?

Ihmiset eivät tee sitä, mitä mitataan. He tekevät sitä, minkä kokevat merkitykselliseksi ja mahdolliseksi.

Kun mittarit alkavat ohjata toimintaa liikaa, huomio siirtyy helposti itse tavoitteesta mittarin optimointiin. Silloin voidaan saada parempia tunnuslukuja ilman, että työ tai sen vaikuttavuus oikeasti paranee.

Tämä on suomalaisen tuottavuuskeskustelun sokea piste.

Mittaamme tehokkaasti sitä, mikä on helposti laskettavissa. Sen sijaan ne tekijät, joista tulevaisuuden tuottavuus rakentuu, jäävät liian usein näkymättömiksi.

title: Meta Tests Muse AI Agent Calls That Are Actually Made By Humans in a Call Center
content:
Last week, Meta executives announced that its much-hyped AI agent, Muse, had a new feature: It could call businesses for you to do things like make a restaurant reservation or a haircut appointment. But in reality, Meta is testing having these calls being made by human beings in call centers, 404 Media has learned.

“We just expanded the @muse beta for outbound calls to US businesses,” Ryan Fox, the principal engineer on Muse posted on X on Sept. 16. Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, posted “we’re expanding our phone beta for muse!” 

Internally, however, the company announced the features to employees and said that it had “added a human agent layer for calls to get completed,” and that “Muse human agent calls [sic] is ready for company dogfooding,” or testing. 

“Muse doesn’t just dial a number. It calls a business on your behalf, handles the conversation, completes your request, and reports back with a transcript and a summary,” the internal message board post to employees, seen by 404 Media, reads. “It also no longer works alone. Muse is now able to hand requests to a trained human agent, who places the call and works it through.”
snippet: Last week, Meta executives announced that its much-hyped AI agent, Muse, had a new feature: It could call businesses for you to do things like make a restaurant reservation or a haircut appointment.

title: South Sudan: Authorities must protect civic space ahead of scheduled national elections
content:
Following the announced dissolution of South Sudan’s Revitalized Transitional Government of National Unity, a decisive step towards the country’s first-ever elections scheduled for 22 December, Amnesty International’s Regional Director for East and Southern Africa, Tigere Chagutah, said:

“Ahead of these long-awaited and historic elections, South Sudanese authorities must ensure that a conducive environment exists for people to vote and stand in elections, including respect for and enjoyment of human rights, and freedom from discrimination and arbitrary or unnecessary and disproportionate restrictions.

“The legitimacy of any election depends not only on whether it is held, but on whether people can exercise their rights freely, safely and equally. For years, Amnesty International and other organizations have documented the repressive tactics deployed by the South Sudanese authorities to silence dissent, detain critics, and restrict freedom of expression and the right to protest.

title: Analysis: Nepal’s $20m ‘loss-and-damage’ claim only covers 0.7% of flood costs
content:
• Nepal’s needs
  • Requests vs pledges
  • ‘Rapid response’

    • The Nepali government has requested $20m from the UN fund for “loss and damage”, following the devastating floods that hit the country in late August.

    This amounts to just 0.7% of the $2.7bn it has estimated in “physical damage” to infrastructure and “economic losses” from the flooding, according to Carbon Brief analysis.

    The $20m request would, nevertheless, make Nepal the fourth-largest claimant to the UN loss-and-damage fund, which is intended to help deal with climate-related disasters.

    Developing countries have already made 176 applications to the UN fund for responding to loss and damage, requesting, in total, $2.8bn to help recover from a variety of damaging events, such as drought, floods and storms.

    Yet, to date, predominantly developed nations have only pledged $0.8bn to support the fund.

    This means requests to the fund are already three times larger than the total amount pledged, raising questions about its potential to respond to emergencies.

    As yet, no funding has been paid out of the fund to developing countries grappling with intensifying and more frequent climate change-induced disasters since it was established in 2023.

title: Russian Fertilizer: Nourishing the Roots of War
content:
Russian fertilizer makers have largely escaped sanctions, despite their importance for revenues, the provision of war materiel, and strategic leverage. There are no sanctions on products entering the US, and the European Union (EU) only imposed curbs in mid-2025.

As a result, the Russian fertilizer industry has enjoyed a booming export market in the EU and US since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. At the same time, the Kremlin’s manipulation of European gas supply has devastated EU manufacturers, enhancing opportunities for exporters.

And the proprietors of these businesses, such as Uralchem’s Dmitry Mazepin and Eurochem’s Andrey Melnichenko, are not neutral businessmen. They are close to the Russian leadership, have been personally sanctioned by the EU, and provide vital explosives for the war.

Russia’s fertilizer industry has become a major economic and military security threat, which Western allies need to tackle.

title: Transformations. A DARIAH Journal launches second issue on “The Past”
content:
How do digital methods shape the ways we understand, preserve and interpret the past? The second issue of Transformations. A DARIAH Journal, dedicated to “The Past”, brings together five articles exploring this question. Following the inaugural issue on workflows, the new issue examines both the possibilities and the challenges of working with historical sources and cultural heritage in a digital world.

As guest editors Agiatis Bernardou and Georgios Artopoulos explain in their introduction, “these contributions suggest that the past is never simply waiting to be retrieved. It must be identified, organised, connected, preserved and interpreted.”

The published articles address topical issues: information extraction from bibliographic data, data migration as a memory preservation process, data feminism in the work with historical newspapers, critical perspectives on historical statistics, the interaction between wikibase and memory institutions collections. Together, they provide novel methodological insights in the spirit of Open Science, making their datasets available for reuse.

title: Could Cuba Become a "Silent Gaza"? U.S. Fuel Blockade Aims to "Asphyxiate" Island: Top Cuban Diplomat
content:
As the United Nations General Assembly opens in New York, we speak with senior Cuban diplomat Carlos Fernández de Cossío, who says the Trump administration is seeking to “asphyxiate the people of Cuba into submission.” On Friday, millions in Cuba lost power in what was at least the sixth major blackout since President Trump cut off fuel shipments to the island in January. The fuel blockade comes on top of the six-decade-long U.S. economic embargo and countless attempts to topple the communist government.

“We will do all we can to stop any nation, the U.S. or any nation, from taking over Cuba,” says Fernández de Cossío, who has served as deputy Cuban foreign minister since 2022.

content:

Successful scholarship applicants are expected to volunteer for at least 4 to 6 hours during the event, in addition to participating in conference sessions and activities. title: Is Latvia “one big training ground” where you cannot pick mushrooms?
content:
The National Armed Forces (NAF) Law defines a military training ground as a geographically designated area of the territorial sea or land territory of the Republic of Latvia, as well as the airspace above this territory, where military exercises, manoeuvres involving the use of training and combat ammunition, tactical training and host-nation support are carried out, the ministry explained.

There are five military training grounds in Latvia:

  • the Ādaži military training ground;
  • the Mežaine military training ground in Kurzeme;
  • the Lāčusils military training ground in Vidzeme;
  • the Meža Mackeviči military training ground in Latgale;
  • the Sēlija military training ground.

    • Latvia also has two military aviation training areas: in Ādaži and Jūrmalciems.

    According to the MoD, the total area of the military training grounds is approximately 43 000 hectares, of which the Sēlija military training ground occupies 24 500 hectares.

title: European experts call for immediate Grade 1 protection and adaptive reuse of British Barracks at Fort Chambray, Malta
content:
A European expert team has released a Report on the preservation of the British Barracks at Fort Chambray in Gozo, Malta. An exceptionally important element of Gozo’s architectural, social and European heritage, the Barracks were constructed at the turn of the 20th century as married quarters for British military families, and are now threatened with demolition to make way for a new five-storey spa hotel, which would incorporate only a reconstructed version of the historic arcaded façade.

The British Barracks at Fort Chambray were listed among the 7 Most Endangered heritage sites in Europe for 2026, in the framework of the 7 Most Endangered Programme run by Europa Nostra with the support of the European Investment Bank Institute. The site was nominated by Din l-Art Ħelwa – the National Trust for Malta.

The European experts recommend protecting the British Barracks through Grade 1 scheduling and pursuing their adaptive reuse, arguing that conservation and economic development can be mutually supportive and that the building can contribute to the future sustainable development of Fort Chambray and Gozo.

title: Technology-facilitated trafficking: How Bangladeshi migrants become victims of recruitment in Cambodia
content:
17,031 Bangladeshi migrants travelled to Cambodia for work from June 2023 to July 2026

Originally published on Global Voices

The Streets of Phnom Penh. Image via Flickr by ND Strupler. CC BY-2.0.

This report features interviews and infographics by Abdur Rahaman, Atkia Fariha, A. K. M. Hasanat Alimoon, Lamesha Akter, and Shanta Akter for the Data Journalism Course at the University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh.

Sajjad Hossain was 23 in 2025, a fresh graduate from Comilla city in eastern Bangladesh, when a job advertisement reached him through a WhatsApp group. It promised data-entry work in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, with a wage several times what he could earn at home, and a middleman handling the visa process. Within one month, he had signed the paperwork, paid roughly BDT 450,000 (USD 3,640), and boarded a flight to Cambodia. Within 48 hours of landing in Phnom Penh, his passport had disappeared into a company safe, and so had the job he had been promised.

title: Ciné-club Nordique: Girl Picture
content:
Le Ciné-Club Nordique consacre son édition d’octobre au cinéma finlandais avec le film Girl Picture (2022), réalisé par Alli Haapasalo. En écho aux thèmes du film, cette séance est organisée dans le cadre de la Journée internationale de la fille, en collaboration avec l’Ambassade de Finlande qui participe à la campagne Girls Takeover. Le Girls Takeover est une initiative mondiale menée par Plan International où de jeunes filles occupent des postes de direction de haut niveau pendant une journée. À cette occasion, une jeune fille sera accueillie comme « ambassadrice d’un jour ».

Girl Picture suit trois jeunes femmes, Mimmi, Rönkkö et Emma, à l’aube de l’âge adulte. Meilleures amies, Mimmi et Rönkkö se soutiennent sans condition et rêvent d’une vie pleine d’aventures, d’expériences et de passion. Emma, quant à elle, a consacré sa vie au patinage artistique et à la réussite. Lorsque leurs chemins se croisent, de nouvelles possibilités s’ouvrent à elles. Entre premiers amours, désir, plaisir, amitié et quête de soi, leurs vies prennent des directions inattendues. Trois vendredis suffisent à bouleverser leur monde.

title: 10 Menettely tietosuojaoikeuksien toteuttamisessa ja pyyntöjen käsittelyssä
content:
Tietosuoja-asetuksessa ei ole muotovaatimuksia pyyntöjen esittämiselle. Tietosuoja-asetus ei kiellä pyyntöjen esittämistä myöskään suullisesti. Rekisterinpitäjien tulisi tarjota käyttäjäystävälliset yhteydenottokanavat pyyntöjä varten, kuten lomake, jolla pyyntö voidaan esittää. Pyyntöjen esittämistä ja niiden käsittelyä voidaan myös sujuvoittaa esimerkiksi kertomalla lomakkeen yhteydessä tietosuoja-asetuksen ja julkisuuslain mukaisten pyyntöjen eroista sekä kunnan suorittamista käsittelytoimista, jotta rekisteröidyn on helppo täsmentää pyyntöään. 

Pyyntöjen esittämiseen ei kuitenkaan voi vaatia pelkästään tietyn yhteydenottokanavan, kuten lomakkeen käyttämistä. Rekisterinpitäjä ei pääsääntöisesti voi myöskään kieltäytyä käsittelemästä pyyntöä, vaikka se olisi tehty muun kuin ensisijaisen yhteydenottokanavan kautta. Rekisteröity voi siis esittää pyynnön myös vapaamuotoisesti. Rekisterinpitäjän tulee joka tapauksessa varmistaa, että rekisteröity on antanut tarvittavat tiedot pyynnön käsittelyä varten ja että rekisteröity voidaan tunnistaa ennen pyynnön toteuttamista.

title: Tutkimus osoittaa: Eläimetkin ystävystyvät
content:
Ihminen on siitä erikoinen eläinlaji, että se haluaa muodostaa sosiaalisia suhteita toisten eläinlajien kanssa. Sama pätee kuitenkin myös muihin kädellisiin, kertoo uusi tutkimus.

Se ei sinänsä ole uutta: jo pitkään on tiedetty, että eri eläinlajit ovat tekemisissä keskenään etenkin, jos siitä on niille hyötyä. Primates-lehdessä julkaistu tutkimus kuitenkin viittaa siihen, että eläimet vuorovaikuttavat keskenään myös puhtaasti sosiaalisista syistä.

Tutkijat kokosivat 1970-luvulta vuoteen 2025 asti tiedot 427:sta kädellisten ja muiden lajien kohtaamisesta. Yleisimpiä tapoja olivat leikkiminen ja turkinhoito, mutta kädelliset myös kantoivat muita eläimiä, käpertyivät niiden viereen, jakoivat niiden kanssa ruokaa tai jopa adoptoivat niitä.

Tutkimuksissa on esimerkiksi havaittu, kuinka lehtiapina silittelee oravaa, gorilla tuudittelee korvamakia ja makaki hoitaa kulkukoiran turkkia, Länsi-Australian ja Oxfordin yliopistojen apulaisprofessori Cyril Grueter kirjoittaa The Conversation -lehdessä.

Osa vuorovaikutuksesta saattaa selittyä sillä, että kädellisillä on luultua laajempi kyky sosiaaliseen joustavuuteen, uteliaisuuteen ja suvaitsevaisuuteen muita eläinlajeja kohtaan, hän arvelee.

title: Romanian Ex-Presidential Candidate Held in €1.1M Fraud Case
content:
Romanian prosecutors have asked a Bucharest court to place former presidential candidate Călin Georgescu and businessman Ionel Rusen in pretrial detention for 30 days over an alleged organized criminal group and a 1.1 million euro ($1.26 million) fraud. 

According to a prosecution filing reviewed by OCCRP, investigators allege Georgescu, Rusen and Italian businessman Massimiliano Arena persuaded a Romanian businessman to transfer money as a guarantee for a foreign credit line that never materialized. Prosecutors say Georgescu initiated the arrangement and introduced Rusen as someone capable of securing the financing.

The victim first transferred 1 million euros and later another 100,000 euros after being told the loan could be increased from six million euros to 15 million, the filing says. Prosecutors detained Georgescu and Rusen for 24 hours following searches that uncovered electronic devices, signal jammers and documents suspected of being false. The filing also cites secretly recorded conversations in which Georgescu discussed buying property in Italy and seeking political asylum, which prosecutors cited in arguing that he posed a flight risk.

title: The Digital Dada Library: Discover the Archive That Preserves the Original Publications of the Experimental Anti-Art Movement Online
content:
Critical theorists like Theodor Adorno may have overreached in claiming that all mass culture is mediocre, mechanized propaganda made to justify the status quo. But that doesn’t mean they were entirely wrong. Over and over we see even the most subversive art, literature, film, and music has a way of being tamed and Bowdlerized. Global mega-corporate industries don’t need to censor what they don’t like; they only need to buy it, rebrand it, or price it out of reach.

So what? Why do we need challenging, independent art when we have endless entertainment? Is the concept a nostalgic, elitist, Eurocentric idea? Artists have justified the need for art since antiquity, with poetic and logical arguments of every kind. But Dada artists of the early 20th century broke ranks, building their movement on the insight that no defense could possibly mean anything when it came to art’s purpose, especially in the face of the technocratic slaughter of World War I.

title: AI anxiety is sweeping the globe — and cutting across party lines
content:
The freakout over artificial intelligence that started in Silicon Valley and led to growing American calls to pause development has swept Western countries.

A new POLITICO Poll finds that pluralities of adults in the U.S., Canada and Europe want to pause AI development regardless of their political leanings — and most believe there’s a real risk the technology could destroy humanity.

Pluralities of respondents in several countries say it’s ok for their country to fall behind others in the development of AI if it means being more responsible and secure when advancing it. And they’re more likely to expect AI will destroy jobs rather than create them. 

This is coming as world leaders are gathering in New York for the United Nations General Assembly and grappling with how to regulate the technology — or not.

title: Six-year-old Chinese girl ‘sets new women’s Rubik’s Cube world record’
content:
Lian Yunzhi solves 3x3 puzzle on several occasions in average time of under 4.5 seconds, according to state media

A six-year-old Chinese girl has set a new women’s world record for solving a Rubik’s Cube in just over four seconds, state media reported.

“Speedcuber” Lian Yunzhi broke the women’s 3x3 average world record twice this month at two World Cube Association certified competitions in Wuhan and Guangzhou, according to state broadcaster CCTV on Monday.

title: Why banning AI in the classroom will not be enough to remedy poor reading skills in a post-literary society
content:
Policymakers are sounding the alarm about AI and social media in schools, as PISA’s latest report confirmed that student performance in reading continues to decline. French Education minister Édouard Geffray lamented the “cognitive destruction” of a generation, while his Spanish counterpart, Milagros Tolón, recommended a focused effort to improve reading because “reading is the foundation of everything”.

The Economist’s editorial board called it a “slow-moving catastrophe”, emphasising that “while machines are getting brighter (… ) teens are getting dimmer”, and pinned blame on the weak, “radical” leftists in university education departments. Meanwhile, the “radical left” is taking meaningful action. On September 2, shortly before the publication of the PISA scores, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced a ban on student-facing generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) use in New York City public schools from pre-school through eighth grade (approx. 4-14 years of age), to be complemented by “twice-yearly AI critical thinking modules for high schoolers, limited AI pilots for a small number of high school classrooms and age-appropriate screen time restrictions”.

title: Bangladesh has lost 900 children to measles – a warning to other countries where vaccine rates have slipped
content:
Almost 900 people in Bangladesh are suspected to have died in a measles outbreak that began in March. Most of those affected are children.

Measles is one of the most infectious diseases known. It can spread rapidly when vaccination rates fall, and the Bangladesh outbreak shows how quickly years of gaps in protection can turn into a serious public health crisis.

The country had hoped to eliminate measles and rubella by 2020. Instead, the pandemic disrupted routine childhood vaccinations, leaving pockets of children vulnerable to the virus. Now other countries where vaccination rates have fallen face a similar risk.

Vaccine hesitancy is probably part of the story here too. During the COVID pandemic, almost half of Bangladesh’s population were wary of getting vaccinated. That same wariness may well have carried over to the measles-rubella jab, with many parents simply refusing to let their children be vaccinated.

Measles has its own set of drivers, too. Poverty, education levels, and how often mothers attend antenatal check-ups all shape whether children in a community end up vaccinated. Add it all up, and childhood vaccination coverage has been sliding for years – down to just 87%.

title: Pisa-tulokset velvoittavat arvioimaan S2-opetusta
content:
Suomen laskevat Pisa-tulokset ovat poliitikoille kuin Harry Potterin Iseeviot-peili: se ei näytä totuutta vaan sen, mitä katsoja haluaa nähdä. Yksi näkee tulosten laskun syynä kännykät, toinen koulutusleikkaukset, kolmas inkluusion.

Jokainen löytää juuri sen syyn, jota on vaatinut koko vaalikauden korjattavaksi. Kukaan ei muuta mieltään, mikään ei korjaannu, ja sama kuvio toistuu seuraavan raportin saapuessa.

Erityisesti maahanmuuttajavastaisten poliitikkojen – kuten perussuomalaisten – peilistä katsoo joka kerta sama kuva: maahanmuuttajataustaiset lapset ovat aiheuttaneet Suomen tulosromahduksen. Niin tälläkin kertaa. Ministeriporrasta myöten annettiin ymmärtää, että maahanmuuttajalapset ovat syypäitä Suomen tuloslaskun jatkumiseen.

Tämä ei yksinkertaisesti pidä paikkaansa. Sen olisi huomannut avaamalla raportin – jo pelkän sisällysluettelon lukeminen olisi riittänyt. Lukutaito heikkeni Suomessa suunnilleen saman verran kuin OECD-maissa keskimäärin. Suomen laskukäyrä on lähes täsmälleen samanlainen kuin esimerkiksi Japanin ja Etelä-Korean, joissa maahanmuutto on olematonta.

title: People Training OpenAI’s AI Fired for Using AI to Train the AI
content:
OpenAI has an army of contractors who read real ChatGPT users’ prompts and other data to help improve the chatbot’s responses. The idea is that the contractors provide an, obviously, human touch to OpenAI’s models. Well, not all of the contractors are doing that. 404 Media has found multiple contractors hired to improve OpenAI’s models have been fired for using AI to train the AI. That’s not great for the models themselves, but there is also obviously a great irony in AI training companies working for OpenAI firing people for using AI when OpenAI’s whole thing is to make people use AI at work.

Some AI models already exhibit signs of “model collapse,” which is where AI models further trained on AI-generated text can become worse and worse. In this case, some of the people hired to partially stop that happening are themselves using AI-generated responses to train OpenAI’s models.

One contractor said they see people using AI “all the time and people are let go for it all the time, it’s pretty much the one thing that will get you kicked off ASAP.” The person said, “in a group of thousands there are tons that have been caught.”

title: No further than the idea stage: defence start-ups struggle to secure start-up funding
content:
Once a company has demonstrated the potential of its technology and development begins to accelerate, securing funding becomes relatively easy. Getting to this point is much harder, meaning that many start-ups never get beyond the idea stage because they lack funding.

For defence-sector companies to develop rapidly, money is needed not only when they have already achieved their first successes, but also at the very beginning – to develop the idea, build a prototype and test the technology. Yet, the funding currently available falls far short of covering all companies’ needs. This means that a promising idea may never progress beyond the initial stage – not because it lacks potential, but because the company does not have sufficient resources to demonstrate that potential.

title: 9 Rekisteröidyn oikeudet
content:
Tietosuoja-asetuksessa säädetään rekisteröidyille – eli henkilöille, joita henkilötiedot koskevat – joukko erilaisia oikeuksia, joiden avulla he voivat valvoa ja hallita omien henkilötietojensa käsittelyä (”tietosuojaoikeudet”). Tietosuoja-asetuksen mukaan rekisteröidyllä on: 

  • Oikeus saada läpinäkyvää tietoa henkilötietojensa käsittelystä 
  • Oikeus tutustua itseään koskeviin tietoihin ja saada jäljennös tiedoista (”tarkastusoikeus”) 
  • Oikeus tietojen oikaisemiseen 
  • Oikeus poistaa tiedot 
  • Oikeus rajoittaa tietojen käsittelyä 
  • Oikeus siirtää tiedot järjestelmästä toiseen 
  • Oikeus vastustaa tietojen käsittelyä 
  • Oikeus olla joutumatta automaattisen päätöksenteon kohteeksi 
  • Oikeus peruuttaa suostumus, johon henkilötietojen käsittely perustuu, ja saada tiedot poistetuksi 
  • Oikeus saada ilmoitus henkilötietojen tietoturvaloukkauksesta, joka todennäköisesti aiheuttaa korkean riskin rekisteröidyn oikeuksille ja vapauksille

    • Rekisteröity ei voi käyttää kaikkia oikeuksia kaikissa tilanteissa. Tilanteeseen voi vaikuttaa esimerkiksi se, millä tietosuoja-asetuksessa säädetyllä käsittelyperusteella henkilötietoja käsitellään.

title: EU and Canada to unveil new partnership, but it may not be ‘associate membership,’ says ambassador
content:
Ottawa and Brussels will announce a comprehensive set of partnerships within the coming year, but the shape of the future relationship is still up for discussion, Canada’s ambassador to the EU said Tuesday.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced during her State of the Union speech last week that the door would be open to Canada becoming “the first associate member” of the EU. But Ottawa has played down the formal nature of that arrangement.

“It was enormously gratifying for Canada to hear that from the president because I think it reflects the fact that Europeans see Canada in the same way that we see Europe,” Jonathan Wilkinson told POLITICO’s Brussels Playbook Live Summit.

“Ultimately, I’m less fussed about what we end up calling it. I’m more fussed about that we have initiatives that are really going to drive prosperity, economic security, and a range of things moving forward,” he said.

title: Using AI to ‘talk to animals’ might make us feel clever – but what, if anything, does it do for them?
content:
As animal behaviorists increasingly use AI in their research, they grapple with how to wield the technology responsibly

I’m sitting in a small boat in Shark Bay, Australia, eavesdropping on a conversation between some of Earth’s most intelligent beings. The motor is off, the turquoise sea is glassy, and Stephanie King and I are motionless, transfixed by the whistles, clicks and squeezy, whirring noises made by the dolphins swimming below us.

If anyone could tell me what these big-brained social mammals are saying, it would be her. Based at the University of Bristol, she co-leads Shark Bay Dolphin Research, one of the longest-running wild dolphin research projects in the world. She has spent thousands of hours watching and listening to this population.

title: Ethiopia’s armed opposition unites against Abiy Ahmed: 5 reads on the country’s political struggles
content:
Seven Ethiopian armed groups have announced a new alliance aimed at overthrowing the government of Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.

The so-called Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival was unveiled in September 2026. It arrives at a time when Abiy is grappling with armed conflict and deepening political and ethnic divisions. There is fighting in the Amhara region between federal forces and local insurgents. Meanwhile, rising tensions in Tigray have sparked fears of renewed war. These are only two flashpoints in a sea of political divisions that war, elections and national dialogue have so far failed to heal.

The Conversation Africa has published extensively on Ethiopia’s attempts to hold the country together. Here are five essential reads.

Ethiopia launched a national dialogue process in 2022 after a stop to a two-year war in Tigray. The process aims to address the grievances that have led to decades of political instability and violence.

title: Varsinais-Suomessa on nyt yli 500 000 asukasta
content:
Varsinais-Suomi vahvistaa asemaansa asukasluvultaan Suomen kolmanneksi suurimpana maakuntana ja nopeimmin kasvavien joukossa. Maakunnan asukasluku ylitti Tilastokeskuksen ennakkotietojen mukaan elokuussa puolen miljoonan asukkaan rajan. Tarkka luku oli elokuun lopussa 500 321.

Väestö kasvoi vuoden takaisesta 3 309 asukkaalla, mikä oli toiseksi nopein kasvuvauhti heti Uudenmaan jälkeen. Varsinais-Suomen kasvu on ollut viime vuosina hyvin nopeaa.

– Varsinais-Suomi on saanut 2020-luvulla 10 000 uutta asukasta kolmen vuoden välein ja edellisen 30 vuoden aikana maakunta on kasvanut lähes koko Kainuun asukasluvun verran, havainnollistaa tietopalvelupäällikkö Antti Vasanen Varsinais-Suomen liitosta.

Varsinais-Suomen asukaslukua kasvattaa muuttovoitto sekä ulkomailta että muualta Suomesta. Nettomaahanmuutto kasvatti Varsinais-Suomen väestöä noin 3 250 asukkaalla edelliseen vuoteen verrattuna ja kotimainen nettomuuttoliike 1 450 asukkaalla.

Ilman muuttovoittoa Varsinais-Suomen asukasluku laskisi, sillä maakunnassa kuolee vuosittain yli tuhat ihmistä enemmän kuin syntyy. Myös syntyvyys on kohentunut hieman kuluvan vuoden aikana.

title: ”Hyvä digipalvelu poistaa työtä, huono siirtää tehtäviä” – Software Finland hakee Suomen parhaita digipalveluita, jotka poistavat turhauttavaa digikitkaa
content:
Suomalaista ohjelmistoteollisuutta edustava Software Finland ry palkitsee jälleen Suomen parhaat digipalvelut. Ehdokashaku on nyt avoinna ja voittajat julkistetaan 5.11.2026. Tuomariston suurennuslasin alla ovat erityisesti selkeys, tuottavuus ja vaikuttavuus.

”Digitalisoitu on, mutta kitkaa riittää”, tuomariston puheenjohtajana toimiva suomalaisen ohjelmistoalan vaikuttaja Riitta Raesmaa kiteyttää.

”Digitaalisia palveluita on rakennettu vuosikymmeniä ja tuottavuus on noussut, mutta ei läheskään niin paljon kuin odotimme. Jos digitaalinen palvelu ei vähennä työtä vaan siirtää tehtäviä omalta organisaatiolta asiakkaille, rima on liian matalalla”, Raesmaa paaluttaa.

Vuoden Digipalvelu -tunnustus myönnetään tänä vuonna jo kahdeksatta kertaa, ja uutta on jako kahteen kategoriaan. Palkinto annetaan parhaalle palvelulle sekä yksityiseltä että julkiselta sektorilta. Palvelut voivat olla suunnattuja joko yksityisille käyttäjille tai organisaatioille: olennaista on, että ne poistavat digikitkaa ja lisäävät tuottavuutta.

Ohjelmistoalan ammattilaisista koostuvan 11-henkisen tuomariston arviointikriteerit on jaoteltu käyttäjän näkökulmaan ja ohjelmisto-osaamiseen. Käytön osalta arvioidaan muun muassa, miten palvelu on lisännyt käyttäjiensä hyvinvointia, tuonut heille iloa, vapauttanut aikaa tai ratkaissut ongelmia. Teknisessä vaakakupissa painavat muun muassa kestävyys, vastuullisuus, innovatiivisuus, toteutuksen laatu ja tietoturva.

”Ohjelmisto-osaaminen on avainasemassa sen varmistamisessa, että digitaalinen kehitys todella sujuvoittaa arkea ja työntekoa. Vibe-koodaamisella on paikkansa, mutta kun tekoälyllä syntyy palveluita hetkessä, osaavan suunnittelun, määrittelyn ja testaamisen merkitys vain kasvaa. Esimerkiksi tietoturvan taso ei välttämättä näy käyttäjälle, mutta jos se on puutteellinen, seuraukset voivat olla vakavia”, Raesmaa taustoittaa.

Vuoden Digipalvelu -palkintotilaisuudessa julkistetaan myös jo 25. kerran Vuoden Ohjelmistoyrittäjä. Arvostettu tunnustus juhlistaa suomalaisen ohjelmistoteollisuuden kasvua edistänyttä ja toimialaa omalla esimerkillään inspiroinutta yrittäjää.

Vuoden Digipalvelu 2026 -tuomariston jäsenet ovat Riitta Raesmaa, Kamoon Digital (puheenjohtaja); Cristina Andersson, Develor Productions Oy; Kalle Heinonen, AI Finland; Jukka Holm, Visma; Sonja Hyrynsalmi, LUT; Tarja Jernström, Microsoft; Ira Keskitalo, Context& Finland; Mette Kontio, Terveyskylä; Janne Lindfors, Barona; Toni Ranta, IBM ja Katja Vakula, Hion Digital.

title: Türkiye’s crackdown on LGBTI groups and activists is part of an escalating rights crisis
content:
On 13 September, I woke in southwest Türkiye to news of a large-scale operation targeting LGBTI organizations and human rights defenders across the country. Since then, police have arrested at least 116 people across 15 provinces following raids on homes, venues and the offices of LGBTI rights organizations. At least 83 people have been placed in pretrial detention and criminal investigations have been launched against more than 160 people. LGBTI rights organisations have reported allegations of intrusive strip searches, insults and humiliation as well as HRDs being held in isolation in violation of their rights. Hundreds of social media accounts belonging to LGBTI organizations and activists, journalists, media outlets and others have so far been blocked or restricted alongside a number of websites. Those affected include Amnesty International Türkiye’s X account.  

As protest within Türkiye builds and international condemnation mounts, it is clear that the Turkish authorities have every intention of intensifying the crackdown

Milena Buyum, Amnesty International

title: Climate Activists Target AI Data Centers & Amazon's Plan to Build Largest U.S. Gas Power Plant
content:
World leaders are in New York this week for the United Nations General Assembly, which coincides with Climate Week. It comes after months of climate-fueled extreme weather around the world, including heat waves in North America and Europe, wildfires in Africa, flash flooding in Asia and a record-breaking El Niño.

Climate campaigner Bill McKibben says that while it’s too late to prevent the climate crisis from unfolding, solar and wind energy are now cheap enough “to blunt its worst excesses.”

We also speak with Kavita Sthanumurthy, a former software engineer at Amazon and a member of Amazon Employees for Climate Justice. She says the artificial intelligence boom is largely being powered by dirty fossil fuel, even as companies like Amazon claim they use 100% renewable energy. “We did our own independent research and found that it was closer to 22%,” says Sthanumurthy.

title: 8 Henkilötietojen jatkokäsittely uusiin tarkoituksiin
content:
Käyttötarkoitussidonnaisuus on yksi henkilötietojen käsittelyn keskeisistä periaatteista ja sillä on keskeinen merkitys henkilötietojen käsittelyn lainmukaisuuden arvioinnissa. Käyttötarkoitussidonnaisuudesta säädetään tietosuoja-asetuksen 5 artiklan 1 kohdan b alakohdassa, jonka mukaan henkilötiedot on kerättävä tiettyä, nimenomaista ja laillista tarkoitusta varten, eikä niitä saa käsitellä myöhemmin näiden tarkoitusten kanssa yhteensopimattomalla tavalla. Säännökseen sisältyy siis kaksi vaatimusta: yksi koskien henkilötietojen alkuperäisen keruun tarkoituksia ja toinen koskien kyseisten tietojen myöhempää ”jatkokäsittelyä” uusiin tarkoituksiin.

On hyvä huomata, että käsittelyn tarkoitus ei ole viranomaistoiminnassa yleensä vapaasti määritettävissä, vaan se perustuu pääsääntöisesti lakiin ja kuntien toiminnassa kunnan tehtäviin ja sallittuun toimintaan. Kunnan toimiala määräytyy kuntalain nojalla. Se, että henkilötietojen käsittelyssä noudatetaan tietosuojalainsäädäntöä, ei poista muun lainsäädännön vaatimuksia. Esimerkiksi tietopalvelujen kehittämisessä on arvioitava muun ohella valtiontukisääntelyn sekä kunnan toimialaa koskevien säännösten asettamat reunaehdot.

title: Trump rejects global entity for AI oversight
content:
President Donald Trump condemned the idea of a global entity to oversee artificial intelligence in his remarks at the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday.

He said the United States “rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control” AI, just a day ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s arrival at the White House for meetings, in which AI could be a major topic of discussion.

The president insisted in his remarks that the U.S. is leading the world in AI innovation and reiterated his argument that the technology’s disruptive or possibly dangerous capabilities are a “hoax.” It comes as Trump has warned that efforts to regulate AI could hamper American efforts and allow China to get ahead.

“We’re leading now over China by a lot and everyone else and we’re going to keep it that way. We’re going to keep it very, very straight and very strong. I’m not going to stifle growth of anything that’s going to be bigger than the industrial revolution,” Trump said. “We will be very careful and that’s why we have a Department of Justice.”

The president also said the name should be changed to “super intelligence,” calling on other nations to drop the use of “artificial.”

title: Game delays for lightning may be annoying, but they save lives – a sports meteorologist explains the risk
content:
When nearby lightning forces officials to delay a big college football game, the backlash from fans can be fierce, especially if the sky over the stadium is still mostly blue.

Sports fans took to social media to complain loudly when nearby lightning forced several game delays on Sept. 19, 2026, including Florida State at Alabama, North Carolina at Clemson, BYU at Colorado State, and Charlotte at Appalachian State. The Alabama delays earned particular anger because there was no rain at Bryant-Denny Stadium at the time.

I’m a meteorologist who studies lightning and lightning safety around sporting events, so I am familiar with the risks and why those lightning rules exist.

My colleague and I documented 262 football-related lightning deaths and injuries in the United States between 1970 and 2023. That included 12 people who were injured by lightning that struck near Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida, after a Green Bay-Tampa Bay NFL game in 2014, and about 40 high school players and coaches who were injured when lightning struck in the middle of a group of players running sprints during football practice in Grapeland, Texas, in 2004.

title: Ensimmäiset tulijat on uraauurtava teos afrikkalaisen diasporan historiasta Suomessa
content:
Professori Leila Koivusen (Turun yliopisto) ja dosentti Anna Rastaan (Tampereen yliopisto) Ensimmäiset tulijat: Afrikkalaisen diasporan varhaisvaiheet Suomessa on ensimmäinen laaja tutkimus Afrikasta ja globaalista afrikkalaisesta diasporasta Suomeen saapuneiden ihmisten ja yhteisöjen historiasta. Se on samalla monipuolinen katsaus ensimmäisinä tummaihoisina eri elämänalueilla vaikuttaneiden yksilöiden kokemuksiin ja siihen, miten heidän läsnäolonsa on muokannut suomalaista kulttuuria ja yhteiskuntaa.

Kasvavalla joukolla suomalaisia on juuret myös Afrikassa, ja useissa maamme afrikkalaisyhteisöissä elää jo kolmannen polven suomalaisia. Silti heidän kokemuksistaan, asemastaan ja afrikkalaisesta diasporasta osana suomalaisen yhteiskunnan historiaa ja kulttuuria on tiedetty tähän asti vain hyvin vähän.

Ensimmäiset tulijat ulottuu ajallisesti 1800-luvun alkupuolelta 1990-luvun alkuun, jolloin afrikkalaisten määrä alkoi Suomessakin kasvaa nopeasti. Kirja kertoo niin Suomeen jo ennen maan itsenäistymistä saapuneista taiteilijoista, seikkailijoista ja lähetystyöntekijöiden kasvattilapsista kuin tänne myöhemmin rakkauden, opiskelun tai työn vuoksi asettuneista ihmisistä.

title: 7 Poikkeusperuste erityisten henkilötietoryhmien käsittelylle
content:
Erityisiin henkilötietoryhmiin kuuluvien tietojen käsittely on lähtökohtaisesti kiellettyä. Tällaisia tietoja voidaan käsitellä vain, jos käsittelylle on sekä jokin tietosuoja-asetuksen 6 artiklan mukainen käsittelyperuste että 9 artiklan 2 kohdassa säädetty erityinen poikkeus käsittelykiellosta. 

Käytännössä kuntien tehtävien kannalta yleisin poikkeusperuste on tietosuoja-asetuksen 9 artiklan 2 kohdan g alakohta, jonka mukaan käsittely on sallittua, jos se on tarpeen tärkeää yleistä etua koskevasta syystä unionin oikeuden tai jäsenvaltion lainsäädännön nojalla. Tällöin sääntelyn tulee olla oikeassa suhteessa tavoiteltuun päämäärään nähden, noudattaa henkilötietojen suojaa koskevan oikeuden keskeistä sisältöä ja sisältää asianmukaiset ja erityiset toimenpiteet rekisteröidyn perusoikeuksien ja etujen suojaamiseksi.

title: UK will aim for ‘single set’ of global AI standards at G20
content:
NEW YORK — British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Tuesday an international agreement on AI led by the U.K. will seek to establish “a single set of global principles and standards.”

Burnham told a meeting with business leaders in New York that AI will be “the primary focus” of the U.K.’s upcoming G20 presidency.

It comes as discussions about global AI governance have shot up the diplomatic agenda, with Burnham telling journalists on his way to the United Nations General Assembly on Monday that the U.K. could be an “honest broker” for a global agreement on how to approach the technology.

It also came shortly before President Donald Trump used his address to the U.N. to assert that the United States “totally rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme” to control AI, in contrast to Burnham’s messaging.

“We want to pick up the initiatives that are beginning to emerge, develop, and bring them into a single set of global principles and standards that are very much about unlocking the full potential whilst guarding against the risks,” Burnham told businesses leaders on Tuesday.

title: Control Resonant review – save New York from paranormal phenomena
content:
PlayStation 5, Xbox, PC; Remedy
A surprisingly conventional game from a famously weird developer, this sequel to 2019’s Control is accomplished but safe

This is an arthouse action game from Finnish developer Remedy, masters of exactly this type of thing. It’s a sequel, however, so not only must it clear the high bar that its strikingly distinctive predecessor has set – it must also ideally arrive with a bushel of new ideas. There are clear and valuable strengths here in character progression and the lustrous presentation of its paranormal world, but Resonant doesn’t feel as enjoyably recondite or expansive in its influences as 2019’s Control did. As you wander New York brandishing supernatural abilities against glowing orange foes, the sad sense creeps in that you might be playing any number of games.

title: The wondrous history of fairy tale art – from wolves and witches to fallen princesses
content:
How do fairy tales, with roots reaching deep into the past, continue to cast their spell on us? This question animates The Art of Fairy Tales by Joanna Ebenstein. The book is a visual exploration of the ever-changing lives that fairy tales take on through the imagination of artists.

In the preface to her essay collection Forms of Enchantment (2018), historian, mythographer and writer Marina Warner invokes the classical idea of enargeia, or “shining vitality”, to describe the vividness through which an artwork seems almost alive. The collection of artworks that Ebenstein presents in The Art of Fairy Tales captures this shining vitality across centuries of fairy tale art.

Each thematic chapter opens with a short introduction before presenting a selection of artworks accompanied by concise but detailed accounts of their artists and historical contexts. Ebenstein avoids a chronological approach, allowing representations of the same otherworldly figures from distant periods to meet on the page.

title: Väitös: Julkinen vaikuttaminen on moniulotteinen ja merkityksellinen osa sosiaalityötä
content:
Suomalaista sosiaalityötä ja sen tekijöitä on kuvattu tutkimuksissa hiljaiseksi ammattikunnaksi, joka vetäytyy julkisesta keskustelusta. YTM Katriina Sirkan väitöstutkimus osoittaa, että sosiaalityössä vaikuttaminen on aktiivisempaa ja monimuotoisempaa kuin aiemmat tutkimukset antavat ymmärtää.

Suomalaisessa yhteiskunnassa on meneillään lukuisia rakenteellisia muutoksia, jotka haastavat pohtimaan sosiaalityön roolia.

Sosiaalityön toimintaympäristö on viime vuosina muuttunut merkittävästi. Muutokseen ovat vaikuttaneet erityisesti yhteiskunnalliset kehityskulut, kuten globaalit kriisit ja hallinnolliset uudistukset. Sosiaalityön on kyettävä vastaamaan näihin muutoksiin ja uudistumaan, jotta se voi toimia vaikuttavasti.

Katriina Sirkan mukaan suomalaista sosiaalityötä ja sen tekijöitä on kuvattu tutkimuksissa hiljaiseksi ammattikunnaksi, joka vetäytyy julkisesta keskustelusta.

title: Statement AlgorithmWatch im Innenausschuss: Bundestag und Bundesrat sollten gegen dieses Überwachungspaket stimmen
content:

Pia Sombetzki, Senior Policy Managerin bei AlgorithmWatch, war als Sachverständige vor Ort und hat in ihrer Stellungnahme erneut kritisiert, dass die Gesetze viel zu weitreichend das Vorhalten von sensibelsten biometrischen Daten gänzlich Unbeteiligter erlauben würden, den Anforderungen des Verfassungs- und des EU-Rechts widersprechen und damit für eine Demokratie unerwünschte Abschreckungseffekte in Kauf genommen würden.

title: Pakistan: Arbitrary detention of Imran Khan’s family and party activists a flagrant violation of human rights
content:
Responding to the arbitrary detention of members of former prime minister Imran Khan’s family, including his three sisters, as well as activists from Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) ahead of the party’s planned protests and march on 27 September , Babu Ram Pant, Amnesty International’s Deputy Regional Director for South Asia, said: 

“The targeting of Imran Khan’s family and PTI party activists is a flagrant violation of their rights to liberty, freedom of expression, association and peaceful assembly. Such actions speak to the severity of the current restrictions in Pakistan. 

“The pre-emptive arrests of PTI members come ahead of planned country-wide protests by the party on 27 September, which government officials have openly vowed to stop. Roadblocks are already being erected in Islamabad. These developments do not bode well, especially given the authorities’ long track record of reckless and unlawful use of force against protesters. A protest cannot be deemed violent before it has even started. Pakistan’s authorities must uphold their obligations under international human rights law to facilitate peaceful assembly and refrain from unlawful measures to thwart these protests.

title: A new project focuses on the viability of volunteer work in northern regions
content:
21.09.2026

  • Share on FaceBook
  • Share on LinkedIn

    • Project manager, PREPAREd | Arctic Centre, University of Lapland

    Senior Specialist, PREPAREd | Arctic Centre, University of Lapland

    The importance of volunteer action for societal preparedness and resilience is growing amid global polycrisis. Current global challenges are deeply interconnected and amplify one another, requiring new ways to approach crises and devise future pathways.

    A new international project, PREPAREd, led by the Arctic Centre at the University of Lapland, examines how volunteering contributes to resilient societies and what support is needed to maintain viable volunteer organisations in a rapidly changing operating environment.

    Volunteers and civil society organisations form a vital, but often less visible, part of society’s capacity to function. Their work can be seen, for example, in preparedness, search-and-rescue activities, environmental protection, and support for local communities on an everyday basis, as well as during times of disruption and crisis. Volunteering is also a central aspect of an inclusive society, offering individuals a sense of belonging and opportunities for agency and lifelong learning.

title: Analysis: ‘Super El Niño’ breaks ‘remarkable’ all-time record
content:
This year’s so-called “super El Niño” has entered record-breaking territory. 

Sea surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific have exceeded the previous daily record set in 2015.

El Niño is a naturally occurring climate phenomenon in the Pacific that reshapes weather patterns around the world and temporarily boosts global temperatures. 

The current El Niño event – which has been underway since June and is expected to last until next year – has been developing faster than any previous event on record. 

The strength of an event is tracked using the “Niño 3.4 anomaly”, which measures how much warmer sea surface temperatures in a section of the central Pacific are than average. 

As of 21 September, the daily anomaly in the Niño 3.4 region stands at 3.11C, surpassing the previous record of 3.08C.

Some scientists, using a different baseline for calculating the anomaly, called the new record a few days before. 

Either way, this is remarkable, in part because of how early in the calendar year it is occurring. El Niño typically peaks in the winter months, most commonly in November or December.

title: AI Safety – Little Hope for a US-China Deal
content:
Concerns over AI safety are growing, fueled by a series of autonomous agent breakouts and fears that humanity is on the verge of losing control to superintelligent AI swarms. 

After Dario Amodei, CEO of AI leader Anthropic, warned about safety risks, US lawmakers have urged new rules to govern AI systems. Amodei also warned that Chinese dominance could present national security risks, provoking Chinese state media to denounce a “Cold War playbook.” But President Donald ⁠Trump has brushed aside ​calls to slow AI development, saying that “very negative forces” exaggerated concerns. Expect any agreement to be narrowly scoped.

title: Burden-EU: understanding the burden of disease
content:
Every breath we take contains tiny particles that are invisible to the naked eye and can harm our health. Air pollution alone contributes to heart disease, stroke, lung cancer, and other chronic illnesses. But how can we measure its real impact on people’s lives? How does it compare with other threats, such as smoking, diabetes or infectious diseases?

To answer these questions, scientists use a measure called the Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY). This combines years of life lost due to premature death with years lived with illness, showing how much of a population’s health is lost to specific diseases and risk factors. This helps governments to see the bigger picture and decide where to invest for the greatest health gains.

Before the launch of the COST Action European Burden of Disease Network (Burden-EU), each country used different methods, making comparisons almost impossible. The COST Action brought together almost 500 researchers from over 60 countries to create a shared framework for carrying out these studies. The result is more reliable, comparable data to inform policies that can save lives.

title: A Principled Approach as the Sands Shift
content:
Creative Commons has been exploring questions around artificial intelligence for a long time: how this profound technological shift might affect people’s motivations to share, whether the intentions behind sharing work before AI became mainstream still hold when we consider how those works are being used now, and how we sustain a thriving commons when the fundamental bargain of the open web has shifted.

Throughout these changes, we have been guided by a commitment to balance creator agency in how people participate in the commons, while preserving the public’s right to reuse. CC licenses operate through copyright, and in many jurisdictions, copyright exceptions and limitations may permit certain AI development and training uses. That can leave people who want to share openly with limited ways to impose conditions, leading some to resort to restricting access instead. This risks pushing us towards an all-or-nothing binary between a free-for-all or enclosure. We fear the end result will be a retracted knowledge commons.

So we’ve been revisiting some fundamental questions:

  • When are norms enough, and when are enforceable conditions needed?
