title: Agiatis Benardou Delivers Keynote and Receives IEEE Award
content:
Agiatis Benardou, President of the Board of Directors of DARIAH, delivered a keynote address at the 2nd IEEE International Conference on Cyber Humanities (IEEE CH 2026), held in Venice, Italy, from 7 to 9 September 2026. The conference brought together researchers, practitioners and representatives of Research Infrastructures working across the intersection of digital technologies, the Social Sciences and Humanities, and cultural heritage.

On 8 September, Benardou delivered her keynote, “From User Needs to Knowledge Ecosystems: Designing Human-Centred Infrastructures for Digital Cultural Heritage”. Drawing on her experience across European digital cultural heritage initiatives and Research Infrastructures, she explored how the field is moving from individual digital tools and platforms towards interconnected knowledge ecosystems. Her central argument was that the challenge is no longer simply to build technically sophisticated systems, but to create infrastructures that become meaningfully embedded in the ways researchers and cultural heritage professionals work, collaborate and produce knowledge.

title: "America, Who Hurt You?": Tony-Winning Performer Sarah Jones on New NY Solo Show & Art as Resistance
content:
Sarah Jones has been described as “a one-woman global village” for her remarkable one-person, multi-character shows. The Tony- and Obie Award-winning writer and performer is best known for her Broadway hit Bridge and Tunnel. She is back in New York with her latest solo performance, America, Who Hurt You?, which is being presented by the National Black Theatre and the Theatre for a New Audience at Polonsky Shakespeare Center in Brooklyn.

America, Who Hurt You? “starts with our history of genocide as a country, our history of enslaving African people, our history of indentured servitude,” says Jones. “This show … is about restoring the history that has intentionally been erased.”

title: Wiki Rookies: Daejeon in-person meetup
content:
From late July to early August, roads across Korea are traditionally packed with people heading off on vacation.

In early August, the Wikimedia community in Korea and neurodivergent participants also took a special kind of vacation of their own: a photowalk in Yeongwol.

Yeongwol is well known for its historic sites associated with King Danjong, as well as for the film The Man Who Lives with the King, which tells a story centered on him.

We’d like to invite you, our readers, to join us as we look back on our time there.

The day of our photowalk, August 1, fell during what was close to the peak of Korea’s summer heatwave.

Since most of our route involved outdoor activities, we first filled up on some refreshing makguksu before heading out.

The tangy flavors of Seoul-style makguksu, the rich meaty broth of Gyeongsang-style milmyeon, and the mild, delicate taste of Gangwon-style makguksu came together to create a whole new world of flavors: Yeongwol-style makguksu.

Our next stop was Cheongnyeongpo, the first place where Danjong was exiled after being demoted to the status of Nosangun.
snippet: From late July to early August, roads across Korea are traditionally packed with people heading off on vacation.

title: Red flags at the start of Apple’s John Ternus era
content:
Tim Cook isn’t the “main character” at Apple anymore. During the company’s keynote presentation on September 9, the long-serving CEO publicly passed the torch to his successor, former hardware engineering lead John Ternus, in time to be the face of a raft of new hardware announcements. There were new Apple Watches, AirPods, iPhones, and, most important of all, the long-expected folding iPhone Duo.

As the announcements progressed, many were watching not just to see what new electronics were coming from one of the mostly highly valued companies on the planet, but also how that company might change under the direction of a new leader. Would Ternus be a continuation of the Cook approach to management? Would new hardware make a comeback after years of tweaks and revenue maximization? Would Apple finally go harder on generative AI after taking a slower and more measured approach to rolling out such features?

title: D.C. Circuit Must Vacate a Drone Flight Restriction That Criminalized Recording Immigration Agents
content:
EFF joined an amicus brief with ACLU, ACLU of D.C., National Press Photographers Association, and Professional Photographers of America to urge the D.C. Circuit to vacate an FAA drone flight restriction that violated the First Amendment right to record law enforcement. This is an important case—Levine v. FAA—challenging the ability of the government to punish drone pilots who record law enforcement officers engaged in official business. 

As we wrote about earlier this year, the FAA issued a flight restriction for drones that had effectively criminalized the recording of Department of Homeland Security officers, including immigration agents from ICE and CBP, and their vehicles (what the FAA called “mobile assets” including “ground vehicle convoys and their associated escorts”) even if the drone was over half a mile away. 

A drone operator, represented by the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, sued the FAA in March [PDF]. But in April, the FAA rescinded the flight restriction.

title: Hanna Karttunen erikoishaastattelussa – tanssia sodan keskellä
content:
Tanssi sodan keskellä haastattelussa Karttunen avaa omaa tarinaansa Ukrainassa ja kertoo kokemuksistaan siellä tänäkin päivänä. Kyse ei ole vain tanssista, vaan elämästä sodan keskellä – arjen hetkistä, kohtaamisista, selviytymisestä ja siitä, millaisen merkityksen tanssi voi saada silloin, kun ympärillä on epävarmuutta. Tanssi voi olla hetkeksi pakopaikka, mutta samalla se voi olla paljon enemmän: tapa pitää kiinni normaalista elämästä, yhteisöstä, identiteetistä ja toivosta.

Karttusen oma suhde Ukrainaan tuo haastatteluun erityisen henkilökohtaisen näkökulman.

Haastattelussa kurkistetaan myös Karttusen poikkeuksellisen monipuoliseen ja kansainväliseen tanssiuraan. Hänen uransa on vienyt hänet 46 maahan sekä maailman merkittäville estradeille, festivaaleille, teattereihin ja televisio-ohjelmiin.

title: Europa Nostra has strategic meeting with Assistant Director-General for Culture at UNESCO Headquarters in Paris
content:
On 16 September 2026, Europa Nostra had an excellent first meeting with Nayef H. Al-fayez, UNESCO Assistant Director-General for Culture, at UNESCO Headquarters in Paris, France. Secretary General Sneška Quaedvlieg-Mihailović and Board Member Laurent Lévi-Strauss, himself a former high-official of UNESCO, represented Europa Nostra at this strategic meeting.

The discussion focused on the centrality of culture and cultural heritage for peace, climate action and the overall resilience of our shared humanity. To champion this strategic goal, we need an even stronger partnership between UNESCO and the European Union, with the vital contribution of civil society.

title: InnoCulture 2026: New Spaces for Culture — Registration is open
content:
What conditions does culture need to flourish? And how can culture create new spaces of its own?

Across the Baltic Sea Region, cultural and creative sectors are navigating rapid technological change, social fragmentation, and shifting political and financial priorities. To stay vibrant, culture needs new spaces in which to create, connect, and contribute.

For its 3rd edition, InnoCulture brings together cultural institutions, NGOs, policymakers, educators, and creative-sector leaders to explore how we build the ecosystems, opportunities, and conditions for culture and creativity to thrive.

Over two days in Hamburg, we’ll approach space on three levels:
→ Create space — the strategic conditions cities and regions can build for cultural work
→ Share space — culture as a driver of inclusion, participation, and democratic resilience
→ Secure space — stronger recognition and sustainable futures for culture in policy

title: Russia’s Baltic escalation playbook: fear is part of the strategy
content:
Russia is promoting a picture of the Baltic region in which NATO is preparing to attack Russia, Baltic governments are heavily militarising, and Russian speakers face imminent persecution. Taken together, these narratives create an atmosphere of permanent crisis in which military escalation appears increasingly plausible. This allows Moscow to exert pressure even without taking overt military action – the possibility of conflict itself becomes an instrument of coercion.

In late 2025, the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) drew attention to the steady stream of Russian FIMI targeting the Baltic countries, noting that they mirror the narratives that the Kremlin used to try to justify its invasions of Ukraine. Recent Baltic intelligence assessments describe a sustained and increasingly organised Russian effort to influence the information environment in Latvia, Lithuania, and Estonia, disseminating anti-Baltic narratives through social media and coordinated cross-platform campaigns.

title: Antti Aaltonen: Oikea kirja oikealle lukijalle -avaus
content:
Erityisasiantuntija Antti Aaltonen Opetushallituksen Lukutaito-ohjelmasta avaa kolmiosaisen ”Oikea kirja oikealle lukijalle” -koulutuskokonaisuuden ensimmäisen tilaisuuden.

Tallenne on ”Oikea kirja oikealle lukijalle” -webinaarista, joka järjestettiin 16.9.2026 osana lasten ja nuorten lukutaitotyön koulutuskokonaisuutta. Tilaisuus oli suunnattu peruskoulun opettajille ja kirjastohenkilöstölle, mutta oli avoin kaikille aiheesta kiinnostuneille. Avauksessaan Aaltonen esittelee päivän ohjelman ja taustoittaa sitä kansallisella lukutaitostrategialla (2021–2030) ja sen kolmella suuntaviivalla, keskittyen erityisesti lukemaan innostamisen teemaan. Lopuksi hän nostaa esiin Suomen Sanataideopetuksen Seuran Hehkuvat sanat -kyselyn (2024–2025) tuloksia siitä, mitä lapset ja nuoret itse toivovat lukemiselta.

”Oikea kirja oikealle lukijalle” -webinaarin järjestivät yhteistyössä Seinäjoen kaupunginkirjaston valtakunnallinen erityistehtävä (SJK Erte), Lupa- ja valvontavirasto, Tampereen, Lahden ja Vaasan alueellista kehittämistehtävää hoitavat kirjastot sekä Opetushallituksen Lukutaito-ohjelman Lukeva koulu -toiminta. title: Protestoimalla vaikutat, sanotaan ilmastoahdistusta poteville nuorille – Hanna Höijeriä se turhauttaa, ja siksi hän kuvaa dokumenttielokuvaa Afrikan ilmastosankareista
content:
”Fuck the politicians: jos he eivät kuuntele, niin ei sitten. Lähdetään itse tekemään tätä hommaa.” 

Se on viesti, jonka opiskelija, ilmastoaktivisti ja elokuvantekijä Hanna Höijer, 22, haluaa sukupolvelleen välittää. 

Hän on kyllästynyt siihen, että nuorille tarjotaan lääkkeeksi ilmastoahdistukseen lähes pelkästään protestointia, vaatimusten esittämistä päättäjille tai somessa toimimista. Periaatteessa se on hyvä asia, mutta samalla herkästi myös vähätellään nuorten omia kykyjä ja jätetään heidät muiden armoille, hän sanoo. 

Höijer näkee, että ihmiset jaetaan julkisessa keskustelussa ilmastonmuutoksen uhreihin ja ratkaisijoihin. Uhreja ovat nuoret, ratkaisijoita taas yleensä ”keski-ikäiset valkoiset eurooppalaiset miehet puvuissa.” 

”Tämä jaottelu häiritsee minua. Joo, nuoret ovat uhreja, mutta se ei tarkoita, etteivätkö nuoret voisi olla myös ratkaisijoita.” 

Siksi hän tekee kollegoineen parhaillaan dokumenttielokuvaa Not Done Yet, joka tuo parrasvaloihin ilmastonmuutokseen konkreettisia ratkaisuja Afrikassa kehittävät nuoret.

title: Fredrik Rysjedal (NO) & Klara Sofie Ludvigsen (NO)
content:
Konstnärerna avser att använda residenset för att tillföra nya perspektiv och förnyad energi till sitt arbete. Båda har uttryckt ett starkt intresse för finländsk konst och kultur och planerar under vistelsen att inte bara skapa nya verk, utan även knyta kontakter med lokala konstnärer och få en djupare inblick i det finländska konstfältet.

Ludvigsens praktik är förankrad i mörkrumsarbete, och residenset kommer att ägnas åt att fotografera och framkalla film, experimentera med material och producera mindre fotografiska tryck. Genom åren har hon utvecklat experimentella och improvisatoriska tryckmetoder, som hon nu ser fram emot att vidareutveckla. Hennes konstnärliga praktik befinner sig för närvarande i en förändringsfas: efter ett decennium av arbete med storformat (4×5″) har hon nyligen börjat använda en Mamiya 7ii (6×7 cm). Denna förändring öppnar nya möjligheter att utforska mer socialt präglade motiv, något som exemplifieras i verket Blå bølge.

title: When Galileo Calculated the Precise Dimensions of Hell in Dante’s Inferno
content:
We venerate Galileo Galilei for daring to speak the scientific truth in the face of severe institutional opposition. He publicly acknowledged that the Earth revolves around the Sun in a time when the Church would rather he didn’t, displaying a bloody-mindedness that he seems to have acquired with age. Decades earlier, in the first stage of his career, he found himself (circa 1588) tasked by the Florentine Academy with calculating the precise dimensions of hell as described in Dante’s Divine Comedy. Dutifully applying himself to this now-absurd-sounding work, he determined that the underworld’s roof had to be centered in Jerusalem, as wide as the radius of the entire Earth, and no less than 600 kilometers thick.

Not that any of this was based on frivolous reasoning. As a model for the dimensions of hell’s roof, for instance, Galileo looked over to Filippo Brunelleschi’s dome, which had topped the Florence Cathedral for a century and a half at that point. Galileo’s calculations of hell’s dimensions contradicted an earlier model proposed by the scholar Alessandro Vellutello. Instead, they supported a model developed by architect Antonio Manetti, whose drawings appear here.

title: Presidentti Stubb ja Norjan pääministeri: Tekoälyn nopea kehitys vaatii kansainvälistä yhteistyötä
content:
Tasavallan presidentti Alexander Stubb ja Norjan pääministeri Jonas Gahr Støre ovat tehneet kansainvälisen vetoomuksen, jonka tavoitteena on varmistaa, että kaikkein kehittyneimmät tekoälymallit pysyvät edelleen ihmiskunnan hallinnassa.

Tähän mennessä vetoomukseen on liittynyt 22 johtajaa 20 maasta eri puolilta maailmaa. Vetoomuksessa ovat sen julkistushetkellä mukana Suomen presidentin ja pääministerin sekä Norjan pääministerin lisäksi Tanskan, Islannin, Viron, Latvian, Alankomaiden, Irlannin, Euroopan komission, Saksan, Espanjan, Moldovan, Turkin, Yhdistyneiden Arabiemiraattien, Bahrainin, Kazakstanin, Singaporen, Kenian, Etelä-Afrikan, Kanadan ja Australian johtajat. Stubb ja Støre kannustavat myös muita maita liittymään vetoomukseen.

Tekoäly on ihmiskunnan suurimpia teknologisia muutoksia. Se tulee vaikuttamaan politiikkaan, talouteen, turvallisuuteen, tieteeseen ja ihmisyyteen. Ihmisten tulee olla kuljettajan paikalla tässä muutoksessa. Meillä on vaihtoehtoja tekoälyn kanssa toimimiseen: voimme kilpailla, tehdä yhteistyötä tai vetäytyä. Oikea vaihtoehto on tehdä yhteistyötä, presidentti Stubb sanoo.

title: Watch: The New Supreme Court
content:
The Supreme Court continues to make consequential rulings in the shadows. I analyzed tens of thousands of case files from the court’s online archives, parsing through filings to separate simple requests for deadline extensions from challenges to long-established constitutional rights. I discovered that in the term that ended in 2025, the justices issued more substantive decisions on their emergency docket than in cases argued in open court. Experts told me this was likely the first time this has happened in the court’s modern history. 

Representatives from the Supreme Court did not respond to my questions. 

Since I reported that story in July, more major rulings have been made on the emergency docket, often called the “shadow docket,” where justices rarely hear arguments and often issue unsigned orders that don’t explain how they arrived at their decisions or even how they voted.

title: Usein kysyttyä: Lainauskorvauksen kuvavähennys
content:
Kuvavähennys on Sanaston työkalu lainauskorvausten tasapuoliseen jakamiseen. Kuvavähennyksen avulla suunnataan suurempi osuus Sanaston lainauskorvauksesta tekstipainotteisten teosten tekijöille.

Käytännössä runsaammin kuvia sisältävien kirjastoluokkien teoksista maksetaan pienempi lainauskorvaus tekstintekijälle. Korvausten laskentaan käytetään kirjastoluokkakohtaista kuvavähennyskerrointa. Lisäksi tänä vuonna Sanasto pilotoi runouden kirjastoluokassa tarkempaa teoskohtaista kuvavähennystä.

Jos kuvavähennyksiä ei tehtäisi, olisi lainakohtainen korvaus kaikille teoslainoille alhaisempi kirjastoluokasta riippumatta, koska Sanasto jakaa kiinteää määrärahaa lainojen kesken.

Kuvavähennys toimii niin, että yli 10 % kuvaa sisältävissä kirjastoluokissa on kerroin, joka huomioi kuvan osuuden teoksessa. Kuvien keskimääräinen osuus eri kirjastoluokkien teoksissa on selvitetty käymällä läpi kattava otanta ko. kirjastoluokan teoksia. Esimerkiksi kertomakirjallisuudesta tekstintekijä saa 100 % lainauskorvauksesta ja sarjakuvista tekstintekijä saa 37,5 % lainauskorvauksesta. Tilitysjärjestelmämme tekee kuvavähennyksen automaattisesti teoksille niiden kirjastoluokan mukaan.

title: Kirjastojen tietoturvaa pitää tukea
content:
Viime viikolla Suomessa uutisoitiin laajasti kirjastojen tietojärjestelmiin kohdistuneesta palvelunestohyökkäyksestä.

Hyökkäykset johtuvat siitä, että kirjastot ovat tärkeä osa kriittistä infrastruktuuria. Ne tarjoavat kaikille avoimen pääsyn tietoon, digitaalisiin palveluihin, kulttuuriin ja oppimiseen. Ne ovat yksi harvoista julkisista palveluista, jotka ovat aidosti kaikkien saavutettavissa asuinpaikasta, varallisuudesta tai taustasta riippumatta.

Asiakkaiden tiedot eivät ilmeisesti ole vaarantuneet, mutta hyökkäys on muistutus siitä, että kirjastojen toimintaan kohdistuu vihamielistä mielenkiintoa.

Kirjastojen tietojärjestelmiin kohdistuvat hyökkäykset ovat erityisen haitallisia, sillä niiden vaikutukset kohdistuvat suoraan kansalaisiin ja heidän mahdollisuuksiinsa saada tietoa ja osallistua yhteiskunnan toimintaan.

Näiden hyökkäysten pitää herätellä päättäjiä siihen, että osana yhteiskunnan tietohuollon kokonaisturvallisuutta kirjastot tarvitsevat kunnolliset resurssit myös tietoturvan ylläpitoon ja kehittämiseen.

title: Sveriges Museer på Bokmässan – om konstens frihet och samtidens uttryck
content:
Foto: Niklas Maupoix

På torsdag finns Sveriges Museer på Bokmässan i Göteborg med två seminarier som på olika sätt tar sig an konstens roll och villkor i vår tid.

Sveriges Museer har i projektet Samtidskonsten sporrar lyft utmaningar och möjligheter för museer att arbeta med samtidskonst. Satsningen har visat att samtidskonsten och dess aktörer ofta fungerar som inspiratörer och utmanar traditionella arbetssätt. Men hur förhåller sig vår tids konstnärliga uttryck till dem inom skönlitteraturen och dramatiken – vad förenar och skiljer dem åt? Deltagare: Gunnar Ardelius, samtalsledare, generalsekretare och författare, Linda Zachrison, konstnärlig chef på Göteborgs stadsteater, Maria Lind, useichef KIN, Kiruna museum för samtidskonst, och Jonathan Brott, poet och redaktör L’Amour – La Mort.

title: EU lawmakers float product liability rules to help avert AI disaster
content:
BRUSSELS — European lawmakers are pushing to expand the EU’s flagship AI regulations to hold American tech companies liable for the risks their most advanced models pose to humanity, according to correspondence seen by POLITICO.

The proposal by four senior lawmakers in the European Parliament would add new rules to the EU’s landmark 2024 AI Act to ensure that companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic could be held liable when their technology is deployed in unforeseen ways.

The move shows Brussels is waking up to a reality in which AI-powered harm is already happening, and risks are multiplying — and marks the first concrete effort within the EU to respond to fears over AI safety that are dominating the global political agenda.

The group is calling on the Commission to introduce an AI Liability Act “to fill the legislative gaps currently existing for these kinds of incidents, so no people or European businesses are left empty-handed against these big providers when they cause harm,” according to a Sept. 16 note to the Commission seen by POLITICO.

title: Black Tesla employees accuse company of fostering racial discrimination in major trial
content:
Lawyers say Black employees at Tesla experienced ‘rampant racism’ that was left unchecked for years at their flagship factory in California

Dozens of Black employees at Tesla’s flagship plant in California said they were subject to racist slurs, unequal pay and promotions, and bullying by supervisors on a daily basis, a situation management did little to nothing to fix.

Their complaints form the basis of a lawsuit brought against the Elon Musk-owned electric car company by the state of California, which began trial with opening statements on Monday.

title: Two more election defeats pile pressure on German chancellor Friedrich Merz
content:
Friedrich Merz’s demeanour was grim as he stepped before the cameras on Sunday evening to address his Christian Democratic Union (CDU) party after two more disappointing state election results. Following what the German chancellor had called the CDU’s “worst defeat in many years” in Saxony-Anhalt two weeks ago, Merz described the result of Sunday’s Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania election as a “disaster”.

His party won just 4.9% of the vote in the largely rural, eastern, coastal state. This means that, for the first time, it fell short of the 5% threshold needed for entering a state parliament.

The CDU found itself squeezed in a contest between the minister-president of the Social Democratic Party (SPD), Manuela Schwesig, and the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD). As in Saxony-Anhalt, the AfD topped the poll but fell short of a majority.

Schwesig’s campaign was criticised for trying to unite all voters opposed to the AfD behind her and thus harming the chances of other parties. But complaining about political opponents trying to win over your supporters is hardly a compelling argument for the CDU.

title: Three T’s will dominate Trump-Xi summit – but expect little movement on trade, less on Taiwan and who knows on tech
content:
When Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping last sat down in May 2026, talk was centered on three T’s: trade, technology and Taiwan.

The latest summit, due to begin in the United States on Sept. 24, looks set to focus on the same set of issues again. The main difference will be that the technology element has been given added urgency by the sudden and rapid shift in developments in artificial intelligence.

What’s less clear is whether the two sides will be able to come to any sort of transformative agreement on that, or any other issue.

The most urgent issue, but also the simplest to solve, will be on trade.

Nearly a year ago at Busan in South Korea, Trump and Xi hammered out an agreement whereby the U.S. agreed to lift some export controls on high-end technology and to reduce the then three-figure tariffs on Chinese goods. For its part, China agreed not to restrict the flow of critical minerals and rare earths to U.S. users.

That pact is now up for renewal. Both sides are likely to want a continuation of the current arrangement, and while there may be some tweaking on the side, the new deal will probably be similar to the old one.

title: Op-ed | Conflict Prevention Has Never Been More Important
content:
To mark the International Day of Peace (21 September), Alex Ballinger MP and Alastair Carr draw on Peace Works – a new report from a coalition of peacebuilding organisations – to argue that a more dangerous world requires the UK to protect the capacity to prevent conflict as well as respond to it.

In July 2011, the UK Government published its Building Stability Overseas Strategy, outlining three guiding principles for conflict prevention: early warning, rapid response and upstream prevention.[1]

Fifteen years on, these principles endure, but the world they were written for is gone. The institutions and assumptions of the liberal international order have weakened and fragmented, replaced by unilateralism, ad hoc alliances, and the arbitrary exercise of hard power.

title: Joshua Farinella on his whistleblowing journey
content:
Joshua Farinella shares his whistleblowing journey, looking back at what happened after he came forward with evidence of food safety, human rights, and labor abuses at a shrimp processing factory in India. With his permission, we’re sharing his words here.

Sometimes you don’t see the impact of whistleblowing until you step back and look at the timeline.

A few years ago, I came forward with evidence about serious problems I had witnessed in the international shrimp supply chain—including forced labor, food-safety concerns, and potential trade violations.

Here’s what happened next:

🔹 2023–2024 — I provided thousands of documents, emails, WhatsApp messages, videos, recordings and other evidence concerning conditions and practices I had witnessed.

🔹 March 2024 — Members of Congress formally sought the underlying evidence and began pursuing the allegations through congressional oversight.

🔹 April 2024 — My whistleblower allegations were raised directly with the FDA Commissioner during a congressional hearing.

🔹 May 2024 — The FDA subsequently took action involving imported shrimp from the facility at issue.

title: Kalatalousalalle tarvitaan uusia osaajia – Turun AMK käynnistää uuden koulutuspolun
content:
Turun ammattikorkeakoulussa käynnistyy syksyllä 2026 uusi kalatalousalan ammattilaisille suunnattu kalan jalostusketjun ja tuotekehityksen koulutuspolku. Koulutus vastaa alan osaajatarpeeseen tilanteessa, jossa kalatalousala uudistuu ja tarvitsee uudenlaista osaamista. Vastaavaa AMK-tasoista koulutusta ei tällä hetkellä ole tarjolla Suomessa.

Kalatalousala on murroksessa. Kotimaisen kalan käyttöä pyritään lisäämään samalla kun kilpailukykyä haastavat kalan tuonti ulkomailta, uusien alalle tulijoiden vähyys ja koulutettujen osaajien puute.

Kehitys kalatalousalla edellyttää nykyaikaisia kalankasvatus- ja jalostusmenetelmiä, automaatiota ja ennen kaikkea laatua, vastuullisuutta ja kuluttajakysyntää tukevia toimintatapoja. Eläköitymisen takia alalta poistuu lähivuosina huomattava määrä työntekijöitä. Alalla tarvitaan osaajia, jotka tuntevat sekä laatuasiat että jalostusprosessin ja kalakaupan vaatimukset.

title: The American Folklife Center Turns 50: See the New Exhibit
content:
—This is a guest post by Stephen Winik, a folklorist in the American Folklife Center. It also appears in the September/October issue of the Library of Congress Magazine.

The American Folklife Center turns 50 in 2026, marking a half century of preserving, presenting and supporting folk culture. The celebration culminates in mid-September with the opening of a major exhibition, “Alive in Many Hands: The American Folklife Center at 50.”

The center owes its existence to the American Folklife Preservation Act of 1976. Congress charged it with safeguarding the nation’s living cultural traditions — everything from fiddle tunes and quilt patterns to holiday rituals, occupational skills and family recipes. These expressions belong to families, ethnic communities, work groups, religious congregations and regions, stretching from the mainland to the Caribbean and Pacific Islands.

Today, the center maintains one of the largest folklife archives anywhere. It exchanges knowledge and expertise with scholars and communities and produces public programs that bring these traditions to life.

title: Kasvu Therapeutics kehittää uutta tapaa hoitaa masennusta
content:
The drug development company Kasvu Therapeutics (Kasvu) put out announcing it has raised €30 million to develop pharmaceuticals for the treatment of major depressive disorder and other brain diseases. The amount is the largest ever raised for a Finnish pharmaceutical development company at the preclinical stage. 

The financing round was led by Norwegian venture capital investor Hadean Ventures focusing on drug development and health industry innovations. Finnish participants in the financing round included Tesi (Finnish Industry Investment Ltd), Innovestor Life Science Fund, Nordic Science Investments, Finnish Drug Discovery Center Ltd, Stephen Industries and University of Helsinki Funds.

The funding helps Kasvu’s lead drug candidate KTX-0141, meant for the treatment of depression, to proceed to initial clinical trials. It is expected to be trialled in humans as early as summer 2027. 

Kasvu’s story is based on long-term work by research groups of Neuroscience Center Research Director Eero Castrén and Professor of Biophysics Ilpo Vattulainen.

Tuulikki Närhinsalo 

Kapsäkin uutuus vie 1400-luvun puoliväliin, Schlimmer-nimiseen saksalaiseen pikkukaupunkiin, mutta vain osaksi, sillä musikaalissa ollaan myös omassa ajassamme. Amerikkalaiskaverukset Doug ja Bud ideoivat ja kehittelevät käsikirjoitusta ja musiikkia Johannes Gutenbergistä kertovaan minimusikaaliin, jolle he toivovat menestystä Broadwaylla.

Anthony Kingin ja Scott Brownin käsikirjoittama ja säveltämä vauhdikas minimusikaali poukkoilee taitavasti Gutenberg-tarinan sekä Dougin – Joel Mäkinen ja Budin – Juha Pulli hyvin nykyaikaisen ajatusmaailman välillä. title: Is this how the world ends? Extinction scenarios are taking over the AI debate.
content:
Aya Ibrahim, who leads national security work for the AI Now Institute, an independent research organization, said that any limitations of AI predictions may get little scrutiny from elected officials. Policymakers have a track record of being deferential when dealing with the tech sector, she said.

“When it comes to tech issues, there’s just this culture of learned helplessness from the same policymakers that sit on energy and commerce [committees] and oversee the FDA and prescription drugs,” topics where they don’t question their right to govern, said Ibrahim, a former Biden White House official. “Suddenly, if you can’t code the model yourself, then you’re not in a position to weigh in.”

title: Is Your City Using Axon License Plate Cameras? We Need Your Help
content:
Cities around the country are ditching Flock’s automatic license plate reader (ALPR) cameras, and replacing them with equivalent cameras from law enforcement contracting giant Axon. That move in large part comes in response to 404 Media’s coverage of how local cops performed lookups in Flock for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and how a cop in Texas searched Flock cameras nationwide to look for a woman who self-administered an abortion.

That brings up questions: what are cities and law enforcement agencies using Axon ALPRs for? And who are they in turn sharing that data with? 404 Media has started to find out, but needs the help of local residents and community members to figure out what is happening across the country.

title: Ukraine’s War Widows Fight for Compensation
content:
Ulyana was living at her parents’ home in Ternopil, western Ukraine, when she was told in 2023 that Vlad, her husband of 17 years and a soldier, had died while at a military base near the frontline in eastern Donbas. He was reported to have killed himself.

“Vlad was the most important person in my life,” Ulyana said as she sat at her kitchen table in a two-bedroom apartment in Kyiv. “We lived in harmony.”

Ukraine pays out compensation to war widows and families of fallen soldiers provided certain criteria are met. But in cases where a soldier’s death has been declared suicide, which is classified as a non-combat loss, there is no entitlement to financial support. After Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, Kyiv announced a one-time payment of 15m hryvnias ($340,000) would be offered to families of soldiers killed defending their country on the frontlines. In 2024, the government introduced a second option, which allowed families to claim 2.27m hryvnias, and is typically issued when a soldier dies while on duty, but not at the front.

title: "Extraordinary Rendition All Over Again": U.S. Deportees Sent to Equatorial Guinea Beaten, Imprisoned
content:
Two men deported from the United States to Equatorial Guinea were arrested by local police forces and transferred to a prison earlier this month, in apparent retaliation for speaking out about conditions they faced in the Central African country. Samson Birhane, who is from Eritrea, and Ahmed Soliman, a gay asylum seeker from Egypt, were both deported by the Trump administration despite U.S. immigration courts granting them protections.

On September 11, police forces arrived at Hotel Bamy in the city of Malabo, where more than two dozen people have been confined after their deportation from the United States to Equatorial Guinea, a country they have no ties to, as part of President Trump’s secretive “third-country” agreements. Birhane and Soliman say they were arrested and taken to prison for speaking out about the inhumane conditions endured by U.S. deportees at the hotel and threats by armed forces. While confined at the hotel, U.S. deportees have decried denial of medical care and legal assistance, and abuses they’ve described as psychological torture.

title: Eight new ECCCH Sister Projects start
content:
Following the Call for Innovative Use Cases for the Cultural Heritage Cloud (HORIZON-CL2-2025-01-HERITAGE-03), ECHOES is delighted to welcome eight more Sister Projects.

CULTUR-ACT – Collaborative Use Case Living Labs Fostering Tools and ResoURces Validation and Adoption in the European Cloud for Next-Gen Digital Heritage Communities Cooperation

CULTURAL.ACT is designed as a real-world proving ground for the ECCCH, leveraging on a community of CHIs and CCIs – of diverse types, cultural heritage domains, disciplines, size and expertise – that agree to collaborate and share experiences in the use of ECCCH tools and resources in core tasks of their own processes and working environments.

HERITWIN – Cultural Heritage Digital Twins

HERITWIN strengthens Europe’s cultural resilience by validating the European Collaborative Cloud for Cultural Heritage (ECCCH) through five real large-scale pilots in Sweden, Norway, Spain, The UK (Northern Ireland), and Greece. The project advances semantic digital twins, eXtended Reality reconstructions, preparedness modelling tools to support conservation, education, public engagement, tourism, and interoperable European data spaces.

title: EU Kids Act Won't Keep the Internet Accountable and Trustworthy
content:
The EU Commission draft law to restrict young people’s access to the internet that it presented last week will come at a high cost: it will put online services behind age gates, expand the use of intrusive age verification, and undermine the privacy of all users. 

The EU Kids Act aims to protect children from risks associated with social media, video games, and AI systems by introducing age-based access rules, safety requirements, and stronger enforcement and oversight measures. It presents itself as building on the Digital Services Act (DSA) and puts into “hard law” some of the safety-by-design measures specified in the non-binding DSA guidelines on minors’ protection. 

The proposal is built around the following elements: social media age “delay”, safety by design, age assurance and parental responsibility, and strong enforcement. Each of these measures are concerning.

title: What deep sea mining could mean for Jamaica’s fisherfolk
content:
‘Any activity that disrupts ocean health could have downstream consequences…’

Originally published on Global Voices

Image of an underwater shot of a vessel with a Jamaican flag on the bottom of its hull, created using Canva Pro elements.

For Jamaica’s fisherfolk, the sea has always been a critical source of food, livelihood, freedom and the future. It’s their pantry, workplace, and cultural centre, but as global companies look to the minerals lying deep below the ocean floor, questions emerge: what will happen to the fishers who rely on these waters when the seabed itself becomes a resource to be exploited?

The way that question is answered could shape the future of Jamaica’s fisheries, and resilience among communities is already bearing the brunt of climate change events. Deep-sea mining may generate sediment plumes, destroy habitats and reduce the biodiversity that cascades through the food chain, placing fisherfolk in the middle of an uncertain ocean economy.

title: Onnistunut vinkkaus koulun ja kirjaston yhteistyönä
content:
Kirjavinkkari Meri Markus Porvoon kaupunginkirjastosta ja äidinkielenopettaja Maarika Toivonen Linnajoen koulusta Porvoosta keskustelevat onnistuneesta kirjavinkkauksesta koulun ja kirjaston yhteistyönä. Haastattelijana Mervi Heikkilä, Seinäjoen Erte.

Keskustelussa Markus ja Toivonen kertovat työnkuvistaan ja siitä, miten heidän yhteistyönsä on rakentunut vuosien mittaan: Toivonen tilaa vinkkauksia kahdeksasluokkalaisten genrevinkkaukseen ja yhdeksäsluokkalaisten kotimaisen kirjallisuuden vinkkaukseen, ja Markus rakentaa niihin kohderyhmän mukaan räätälöidyn, monipuolisen kirjasetin. Puhutaan myös vinkkauksen käytännön haasteista, kuten aikataulujen sovittamisesta koulun ja kirjaston kesken, sekä siitä, mitkä genret ovat nuorten suosiossa juuri nyt. Lopuksi keskustelussa nousee esiin ideoita yhteistyön kehittämiseksi, kuten pidennetyt laina-ajat kouluvinkkauksen yhteydessä ja kirjavinkkauksen tuominen sosiaaliseen mediaan.

title: Vetoomus kaikkein kehittyneimpien tekoälymallien hallinnan puolesta
content:
Syyskuu 2026

Tekoäly on voimakas teknologia. Sillä on potentiaalia parantaa ihmisten elämää, edistää tiedettä ja vahvistaa talouksiamme.

Samalla huipputason tekoälymallien nopea kehitys aiheuttaa vakavia turvallisuusriskejä, ellei kehitystä hallita asianmukaisesti.

Viime aikoina on havaittu, että kehittyneet tekoälyjärjestelmät ovat kiertäneet niiden testauksessa käytetyt suojatoimet, hyödyntäneet haavoittuvuuksia ja päässeet luvattomasti reaalimaailman järjestelmiin.

Johtavat tutkijat ja tekoäly-yhtiöiden johtajat varoittavat, että kehityksen vauhti saattaa ylittää kykymme hallita esiin nousevia riskejä.

Jotta tekoälyn hyödyt voidaan saavuttaa, yritysten, hallitusten ja yhteiskunnan on toimittava nyt. Meidän on puututtava näihin riskeihin ja vahvistettava valvontaa ilman, että kasvatamme samalla maiden välisiä eroja tekoälyn hyötyjen saatavuudessa.

Tekoälyn on pysyttävä ihmisten ohjauksessa, valvonnassa ja hallinnassa. Sitä on kehitettävä ja hyödynnettävä kansainvälisen oikeuden mukaisesti.

Kannatamme siksi viimeaikaisia aloitteita, joilla pyritään hallitsemaan kehittyneisiin teknologioihin liittyviä riskejä.

title: 22 countries back call to keep AI ‘under human control’
content:
NEW YORK — Several European countries were among a group of 22 nations that adopted a declaration Monday saying that artificial intelligence “must remain under human direction, oversight and control” and suggesting to create a global supervisory regime.

The declaration, adopted on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly this week, acknowledged AI’s “potential to improve lives, advance science and strengthen our economies” but warned that “the rapid development of frontier AI models poses serious risks to safety and security if not appropriately managed.”

The push comes ahead of the meeting of U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, the leaders of the world’s leading AI-developing nations, in Washington Thursday.

Neither the U.S. nor China are part of the new declaration. But Finnish President Alexander Stubb, one of the main organizers of the document, told POLITICO that he hopes to create “momentum” and get more actors on board: “I think it will be in the interest of both China and the United States to have some kind of guardrails. And our message here is that we need human intervention, so humans need to be in charge,” he said in an interview.

title: Stop relying on AI chatbots for customer care, UK banks and energy firms told
content:
Citizens Advice says providers of essential services such as energy, banking, phone and internet should guarantee the ‘right to talk to a human’

Stop relying on AI chatbots for customer care and guarantee the “right to talk to a human”, Citizens Advice has urged essential service providers, as research found they wasted time, caused stress and delayed problem solving for more than half of users.

The spread of the AI-powered systems to provide help about the provision of vital services such as energy, banking, phones and internet, is making it harder for millions of already digitally excluded people to handle snags, according to the frontline charity that last year provided more than 2.7 million people with one-on-one help in England and Wales.

title: ‘Small, flowering islands’: German city reveals how nature thrives when neighbours care for street tree beds
content:
When Olivia Besters began caring for the patch of soil beneath the chestnut tree outside her home in Freiburg, Germany, more than 35 years ago, biodiversity was not on her mind.

“It was the optics,” she told me. The ground was compacted and littered with trash and dog “legacies”. Besters simply wanted the space directly outside her front door to look nicer. “Everything else came much later,” she said. “Thirty-five years ago, no one talked about climate change or insect decline.”

Over time, one tree bed expanded into 36 across Besters’ neighbourhood of Herdern. So deep is her commitment to her tree beds that her children gifted her a bike trailer to cart around her watering system, her phone is filled with stunning pictures of the flowers growing in her tree beds, and she has been nominated for city-wide engagement awards.

As towns and cities grow, biodiversity is being squeezed into ever smaller spaces while people experience a progressive loss of everyday contact with nature. Street tree beds – and the practice of caring for them – offer cities a way to counter urban biodiversity loss while enriching people’s connection with nature in their neighbourhoods.

title: Could AI really kill all humans? Most scenarios require physical access, making AI armageddon unlikely
content:
In August 2026, an experiment using “frontier”, or cutting edge, artificial intelligence models went further than planned.

An AI agent (a system that performs tasks autonomously) fabricated online identities in order to pressurise a human to insert malicious computer code into software. The agents had been tasked with solving a cybersecurity challenge by human operators, but they hadn’t been instructed to do anything like this.

The attempt was carried out by an agent based on Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5 AI model. During the experiment, the AI agents were given open internet access, with safety filters switched off. The action ultimately failed, and there was no evidence that any real world harm occurred. But the fact that it happened at all, autonomously and unprompted by a human, was something novel and notable.

It’s tempting to draw a straight line from incidents like this to the doomsday scenarios that dominate public conversation about AI: a system that slips its constraints, decides humanity is an obstacle and moves against us.

Talotekniikka on muuttunut perusteellisesti niiden vuosikymmenten aikana, jotka diplomi-insinööri Ilkka Salo on viettänyt alan parissa. Lämmöllä-lehden laajassa henkilöhaastattelussa Salo nostaa esiin yhden ajatuksen, joka on kulkenut mukana läpi hänen uransa: talotekniikka ei ole ensisijaisesti laitteita, putkia, kanavia tai energiankulutusta. Sen tehtävänä on luoda ihmisille terveelliset, turvalliset ja miellyttävät olosuhteet.

title: Kiusaaminen alkaa kauan ennen kuin se näyttää kiusaamiselta, sanoo tutkija
content:
Uudet tutkimustulokset osoittavat, että lasten ja nuorten keskinäiseen kiusaamiseen herätään liian myöhään. Kun asia tunnistetaan, ryhmässä on voinut olla pitkään käynnissä ilmiöitä, jotka ovat luoneet pohjan ulossulkemiselle, häirinnälle ja väkivallalle. Aikuisilla onkin keskeinen rooli varhaisessa tunnistamisessa.

"Kiusaaminen ei synny tyhjästä. Sitä edeltävät usein pienet, mutta merkitykselliset tilanteet, joissa lapset ja nuoret alkavat arvottaa, vertailla ja sulkea toisiaan ulkopuolelle. Juuri näihin hetkiin pitäisi kiinnittää nykyistä enemmän huomiota", Oulun yliopiston uuden oppituolin, nuorisotutkimuksen, professori Tuija Huuki kertoo tiedotteessa.

Tutkimus haastaa myös yleisen käsityksen siitä, että kiusaaminen johtuisi ensisijaisesti tietyistä "kiusaajista" tai "pahoista lapsista". Tulokset viittaavat siihen, että tavalliset lapset ja nuoret voivat tietyissä olosuhteissa alkaa vahingoittaa toisiaan.

Riski kasvaa erityisesti silloin, kun lasten ja nuorten väliset suhteet jäävät ilman aikuisen ohjausta.

title: "War on the Press": Trump Bans CNN, MS NOW & Politico from White House over Critical Coverage
content:
News organizations CNN, MS NOW and Politico are suing the Trump administration over the banning of their reporters from the White House on Friday. Their credentials were confiscated or deactivated when they attempted to enter White House grounds over the weekend. Trump’s decision is “sending the message that if you write stories that are critical of the president, you’re going to lose your access,” says Katie Fallow, a deputy litigation director at Columbia University’s Knight First Amendment Institute, where she focuses on threats to freedom of speech and of the press. “The real victims of this war on the press are members of the public, which are entitled to know about what their government is doing.”

Fallow says the White House press briefing room is a “public forum” and that “the courts have said repeatedly the government is not allowed to kick people out of that forum based on their viewpoint.”

title: The commodification of Indigenous cultures and traditions
content:
All too often, Indigenous traditions are extracted, repackaged, or seized for someone else’s gain

Originally published on Global Voices

A Huipil, Kaqchikel Maya, Patzun textile displayed in the Textile Museum of Canada, circa late 20th to early 21st c. Such textiles are an important Maya tradition and are still made by Maya weavers today. Image from Wikimedia Commons. CC0.

This post is part of Global Voices’ August 2026 Spotlight series, “Indigenous Rights.” This series offers insight into the lives and experiences of Indigenous peoples to build connections across regions, center Indigenous experiences, and share the stories of leaders, activists, community members, and more. You can support this coverage by donating here.

For many Indigenous communities, the traditions, art, and ceremonies are the backbone of their shared identity, essential for marking important milestones, fostering a sense of community, and passing on histories to the younger generation. However, all too often, these traditions are extracted, repackaged, sold, or seized for someone else’s gain.

title: Inari Mykkänen: Lapsen oikeuksiin tutustuminen kirjavinkkauksen ja sanataiteen keinoin
content:
Inari Mykkänen Espoon kaupunginkirjastosta pitää puheenvuoron ”Minulla on oikeus lukea: lapsen oikeuksiin tutustuminen kirjavinkkauksen ja sanataiteen keinoin”. Tallenne on ”Oikea kirja oikealle lukijalle” -webinaarista, joka järjestettiin 16.9.2026 osana lasten ja nuorten lukutaitotyön koulutuskokonaisuutta.

Mykkänen esittelee Espoon kaupunginkirjastossa vetämänsä ”Minulla on oikeus” -sanataidetyöpajan, joka yhdistää kirjavinkkauksen, sanataiteen ja lapsen oikeuksiin tutustumisen. Työpaja on suunnattu 5.–6.-luokkalaisille, mutta sen teemat sopivat myös muille alakoululaisille. Puheenvuorossa käydään läpi YK:n lapsen oikeuksien sopimusta (1989) ja sen neljää yleisperiaatetta sekä esitellään konkreettisia kirjaesimerkkejä, jotka avaavat eri oikeuksia lasten tarinoiden kautta – esimerkiksi syrjimättömyyttä (Amari ja yön veljet), lapsen oikeutta suojeluun sodassa (Ette tiedä mitä sota on) ja oikeutta lepoon ja leikkiin (Hereiset: Yön salaisuus). Lopuksi Mykkänen esittelee vinkkauksen päätteeksi tehtävän sanataidetehtävän, jossa oppilaat kirjoittavat ja kuvittavat oman ”Minulla on oikeus” -julisteensa.

title: EU pressures Big Tech to go green with new data center sustainability label
content:
BRUSSELS — Brussels on Monday unveiled an environmental rating scheme for data centers that power artificial intelligence, a move the EU’s energy chief described as the first step in pressuring tech giants into aligning with the continent’s climate efforts.

The new rules, which will apply from August 2027, oblige big data centers to display a label grading them on their energy efficiency, water usage and clean power uptake on a scale of A to G, much like the EU’s influential appliances ranking.

“This will add a lot of transparency and hopefully provide the incentives for these data centers to be as sustainable as possible,” said Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen in an interview with POLITICO ahead of the label’s presentation. 

The new label is optional for smaller data centers, “but later we are also going to introduce minimum performance standards which, of course, will put more pressure on those who may not voluntarily wish to be as sustainable as we want them to,” he added.

title: Nvidia boss says there is ‘0% chance’ AI destroys the world by 2030
content:
Jensen Huang dismisses warnings from former Anthropic researcher and others as ‘doomsday narratives’

The boss of the chipmaker Nvidia has said AI will not develop to a point that will lead to the extinction of the human race within a few years, rejecting such assertions as overblown “doomsday narratives”.

Jensen Huang, the co-founder and chief executive of the $5tn AI chipmaker, said the claims made on social media by the former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon that AI could become “superhuman” and kill off humanity within the decade were “irresponsible”.

title: From French outpost to Euro-Canadian corridor? Why Carney and Macron met in Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon
content:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney did not need to cross the Atlantic to meet Emmanuel Macron on French soil over the weekend. Instead, he joined the French president in Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, just 25 kilometres off Newfoundland.

It was the first official visit to the archipelago by a Canadian prime minister.

The visit brought together a contentious shared history, Canada’s rapprochement with Europe and Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon’s search for new development opportunities.

Covering 242 square kilometres and home to around 6,000 people, the archipelago rarely attracts international attention. Yet its location gave the weekend meeting particular significance as France and Canada seek closer ties amid growing tensions with the United States.

After repeatedly threatening to make Canada a 51st state, U.S. President Donald Trump recently posted a map depicting an expanded U.S. encompassing Canada, Greenland and Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon.

Evidence of Indigenous presence in Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon dates back nearly 5,000 years. It later attracted European explorers, including Frenchman Jacques Cartier in 1536.

title: Forgotten Mozart notebook reveals how a young woman learned to compose
content:
A small notebook found in the Bibliothèque Nationale de France (the national library of France) has turned out to be one of the most important Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart discoveries in decades.

The 44 pages of the notebook document composition lessons that Mozart gave in Paris in 1778 to Marie-Louise-Philippine de Bonnières de Guînes, a highly accomplished young aristocratic harpist. The manuscript was recognised in February 2026 by François-Pierre Goy, a curator in the library’s music department who recognised Mozart’s handwriting in the unattributed notebook. Laurence Decobert, a specialist in Mozart’s manuscripts, agreed with him and Armin Brinzing, director of the Bibliotheca Mozartiana in Salzburg, later authenticated the document.

The notebook lets readers follow Mozart’s teaching from one exercise to the next. It also preserves something that composer-centred histories often miss: the musical work taking place around him, in this case by a young woman.

title: POROKYLÄN LEIPOMO SELVITTI LEIVÄN KOTIKÄYTÖN YMPÄRISTÖVAIKUTUKSET – KULUTTAJIEN TAVAT VAIKUTTAVAT SELVÄSTI PÄÄSTÖIHIN
content:
Porokylän Leipomo tilasi Karelia-ammattikorkeakoulun opinnäytetyönä toteutetun tutkimuksen, jossa selvitettiin leivän kotikäytön eli säilytyksen, voileipien valmistuksen ja hävikin ympäristövaikutuksia. Tutkimuksen teki Evelina Meski osana Sustainability Management -koulutusohjelman ylempää AMK-tutkintoa. Tulokset osoittavat, että kotikäytön vaiheen kokonaisvaikutukset ovat suhteellisen pieniä, mutta kuluttajien käyttäytymisellä on niihin selvä vaikutus.

Tutkimuksessa tarkasteltiin Porokylän Leipomon kolmea päätuoteryhmää: perinteistä ruislimppua, palaleipää ja gluteenitonta leipää. Kuluttajien säilytys-, valmistus- ja hävikkitietoja kerättiin kyselytutkimuksella, johon vastasi yhteensä 232 henkilöä. Kerättyä aineistoa käytettiin elinkaariarvioinnin (LCA) lähtötietoina, ja laskenta toteutettiin SimaPro-ohjelmistolla Ecoinvent-tietokantaa hyödyntäen.

Tutkimuksessa tarkasteltiin, miten leipää säilytetään huoneenlämmössä, jääkaapissa tai pakastimessa, sekä miten sitä valmistetaan esimerkiksi leivänpaahtimessa, uunissa, mikroaaltouunissa tai airfryerilla. Lisäksi kerättiin tietoa ruokahävikin määrästä ja lajittelusta sekä kotitalouksien sähkönkäytöstä.

title: Google hit with €403M privacy fine over handling of user location data
content:
The Irish data privacy authority fined Google €403 million on Monday over how it has been gathering location data from users.

This is the fourth largest fine ever issued by the Irish regulator and its first major penalty against Google. Ireland is charged with enforcing the European Union’s privacy rules against many of the world’s tech giants that have their European headquarters in Ireland.

The decision concludes an inquiry that was opened in 2020 by the Irish Data Protection Commission (DPC), following complaints from consumer organizations across the EU over how Google processed people’s location data and the transparency around that processing. 

Google infringed the General Data Protection Regulation, the EU’s landmark laws, on four counts, said Ireland’s three privacy commissioners Des Hogan, Dale Sunderland and Niamh Sweeney. The issues concerned how Google processed and retained location data in its Web & App Activity, Location History and Location Accuracy functions, as well as transparency.

The complaints from consumer groups alleged that Google had used dark patterns and unfair practices to incite users to enable features that shared their location data.

title: EU budget needs taxes governments aren’t already raising, Costa says
content:
DUBLIN — Governments will be more likely to back new EU taxes for the bloc’s next seven-year budget if they raise money that national governments are not already collecting, European Council President António Costa said.

In an interview with POLITICO, Costa set out for the first time what he gathered from leaders during his tour of 25 capitals on one of the thorniest issues in the talks: how to build support towards new EU levies — known as “own resources” — that would generate fresh revenue to the budget.

The answer will help determine whether EU governments can agree on a budget by the end of the year — before 2027’s elections in France, Italy, Spain and Poland threaten to derail the talks — without either cutting spending on new priorities or asking national governments to pay more.

“If we don’t create new own resources, we need to ask [for] more money from the member states,” Costa said. “We know that we need to keep the national contributions at a reasonable limit. For this, we need to have a credible basket of new own resources.”

title: Mostly Harmless
content:
Mostly Harmless ist das erste große Event, das die Magrathea Laboratories ausrichten.

Mostly Harmless – kurz MHL – ist ein Wochenende für alle, die gerne ausprobieren, gestalten, diskutieren und gemeinsam Neues entstehen lassen. 2026 steht die Veranstaltung unter dem Motto „Follständig Harmlos – experimentieren, diskutieren und hacken“.

„Follständig“ verbindet den regionalen Karnevalsgruß „Fölsch foll“ mit dem bekannten „Mostly Harmless“-Motiv aus Douglas Adams’ Per Anhalter durch die Galaxis. Austragungsort ist die Konrad-Zuse-Stadt Hünfeld (Zuses Wahlheimat) – ein passender Ort für ein Wochenende zwischen Technik, Kreativität und neuen Ideen.

Ob Hackspace, IT-Szene, Kultur, Maker-Community oder einfach neugierig: Die MHL bringt Menschen zusammen, die Lust haben, voneinander zu lernen, gemeinsam zu tüfteln und neue Perspektiven zu entdecken.

title: How two elections reshaped the India–Bangladesh border
content:
Push-in attempts by BSF stretch across Bangladesh’s land border, hitting all four edges of the map

Originally published on Global Voices

India–Bangladesh Friendship Gate at the Tamabil-Dawki border in northeast Bangladesh. Image via Wikipedia by Ankan. CC BY-SA 4.0.

This report features interviews and infographics by Amatullah Sumaya, Aronee Ayub, Nusaiba Nawaz, Sampoorna Ganguly, and Sayeeda Nowshin for the Data Journalism Course at the University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh.

A 55-year-old physically challenged stranger appeared on the Bangladesh side of the India-Bangladesh border in Chapainawabganj in June 2026. By the time Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) reached him, a crowd had gathered around him.

He could not hold a pen — not because he did not know how to write, but because he had no fingers with which to hold it.

“The matter came to our attention after Shreejib Kumar Singh was found on the Bangladesh side of the border in the Chapainawabganj area,” the officer-in-charge of Gomastapur Police Station told Global Voices in a WhatsApp interview in August, recounting how the incident was reported to police.

title: Global Poll: People Still Want the UN—But Want It to Deliver
content:
Ahead of the UN General Assembly’s high-level debate, a 20-country survey finds strong support for international cooperation despite widespread anxiety about wars and the future.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | 20 September 2026 (IDN) — The United Nations may be struggling with wars it cannot stop, divisions among the major powers and growing doubts about the international order. But a new global poll suggests that people are not ready to give up on either the UN or international cooperation.

They do, however, expect more.

A survey released by the United Nations Foundation on 17 September found that 57 per cent of respondents were worried about the future, while nearly nine in ten believed that even the world’s most powerful countries need the international system rather than trying to confront today’s problems on their own.

Only 13 per cent regarded the United Nations as outdated and no longer necessary.

But 52 per cent said the organisation remains necessary, even as it struggles to deliver results.

title: Digital Tribulations 25: Building Technological Sovereignty from Below, The Experience of Argentine Cooperativism – Interview with Cecilia Muñoz from Código Libre
content:
The introduction of Digital Tribulations, a series of intellectual interviews on the developments of digital sovereignty in Latin America, can be read here and the entire series can be found here.

During the month I spent in Buenos Aires, the last city I visited before finally flying back to Europe, I managed to get a firsthand look at its famous cooperativist scene, which extends to platforms. By “famous” I of course mean a niche that has accompanied platform studies since the sharing economy: platform cooperativism. I first came across it through the pioneering work of Trebor Scholz, and I became more familiar with it thanks to the prolific scholarship of my Brazilian friend Rafael Grohmann. He was the one who gave me Cecilia’s contact, along with the phone number of a fellow Italian, Stefano Tortorici, who is writing his PhD on platform cooperativism. As two Italian researchers in our semi-nomadic phase, I bonded with Stefano and ended up hanging out with his numerous artistic housemates, who shared a house not far from the gentrified Palermo neighborhood.

title: Disappearance of 2 Journalists in Djibouti Raises Concerns for Their Safety
content:
The Committee to Protect Journalists said Sunday that it is “deeply concerned” by reports that South African investigative journalist Micah Reddy and local fixer Kooki Mahmoud have gone missing in Djibouti, and urged authorities “to immediately clarify their whereabouts and ensure their safety.”

Contact with Reddy, the African coordinator for the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ), and Mahmoud, a Djibouti-based journalist, was lost Saturday at approximately 1 p.m. local time, said an ICIJ statement. The statement, issued Sunday, said ICIJ is gravely concerned for their safety and authorities in Djibouti have not so far responded to its requests for information.

“We are calling on the government of Djibouti to: Immediately clarify Reddy and Mahmoud's whereabouts and confirm their well-being; Launch a prompt, transparent investigation into their disappearance; Keep their families, colleagues and employers fully and promptly informed,” the ICIJ statement said.

title: Nepal could show the world how to recover sustainably from a major disaster
content:

But now is the time to pay careful attention to community-centred lessons from past disasters as complex planning decisions are made about recovery and reconstruction that will shape long-term outcomes.

Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority recently released a Rapid Disaster Needs Assessment (RDNA) highlighting many of the challenges facing disaster-affected Nepalis, including the approximately 33,000 who have lost their homes.

As Nepal prepares long-term recovery and risk-reduction strategies, we offer insights from our collaborative research about post-disaster reconstruction and displacement following Nepal’s 2015 earthquake, as well as ongoing mountain hazards, to highlight areas of concern for the country’s affected communities.

title: From the streets to the ballot box: What Hungary can teach Serbia
content:
Orbán’s machine seemed invincible — until a grassroots movement cracked the psychological trap of fear

Originally published on Global Voices

Péter Magyar's speech at the convening of the National Assembly in Budapest, Hungary, on May 9, 2026. Photo by Elekes Andor via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0).

This article by Tjaša Feher was first published in Serbian on Istinomer.rs on September 2, 2026. An edited version is republished here under a content-sharing agreement between Global Voices and the Center for Research, Transparency and Accountability (CRTA).  

As Serbia gears up for what many already describe as a historic election scheduled for October 18, the challenge is not simply whether an entrenched government can be defeated, but whether almost two years of student-led mobilisation can translate into electoral power.

The political crisis that followed the November 2024 Novi Sad railway station canopy collapse has produced something Serbia has not seen for years: sustained civic mobilisation, new networks of trust and participation by large numbers of people outside conventional opposition structures.

title: Trump declares victory in Greenland, but the deal exposes a deeper crisis of trust
content:
US President Donald Trump is already presenting the new security agreement between the United States, Denmark and Greenland as a personal triumph.

By his telling, Washington has secured permanent control over Greenland’s security and the power to prevent adversaries from establishing military bases or making sensitive investments there.

The Prime Minister’s Office of Denmark describes a different bargain: stronger Arctic security that preserves the Kingdom of Denmark’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as Greenlanders’ right to self-determination.

Yet the political bargain is already visible. Trump gets the spectacle of power – or as a US correspondent for Danish newspaper Politiken said, “he was allowed to take a victory lap on social media”. Denmark and Greenland keep nominal sovereignty. NATO avoids an immediate rupture. Each party can declare success.

That is the optimistic reading. The more troubling one is that the agreement rewards months of coercion against an ally. It normalises a sphere-of-influence politics in which smaller states remain legally sovereign but face pressure to accept strategic subordination.

title: Africa’s Public-Sector Reforms Need Leaders, Not Only Technical Expertise
content:
The African Capacity Building Foundation and the Gates Foundation are expanding a programme designed to help officials turn sound policies into lasting institutional change.

By Jeffrey Moyo

HARARE, Zimbabwe | 19 September 2026 (IDN) — African governments must invest more seriously in leadership development if ambitious public-sector reforms are to produce lasting results, according to the African Capacity Building Foundation (ACBF) and the Gates Foundation.

The two organisations made the case during a 3 September webinar, “Leading Public Sector Transformation in Africa: Leadership Lessons from the LEAPS Programme”. The discussion examined how stronger leadership could help governments overcome resistance to reform, improve public financial management and turn policy initiatives into measurable institutional gains.

Mamadou Biteye, ACBF’s Executive Secretary, said public-sector reform in Africa was rarely held back by a shortage of good ideas.

“More often, the real challenge is our ability to lead change by bringing people together, building trust, overcoming resistance, and sustaining momentum,” he said.

title: “Our Dear Friend Umar”: How We Uncovered That a Russian Oligarch Bankrolled Donald Trump Jr.’s Wedding
content:
My colleagues and I had been digging for days. We’d heard a rumor that a Russian oligarch close to President Vladimir Putin named Umar Kremlev had attended Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding this past May in the Bahamas. But to confirm that, we needed visual proof. 

First, we scoured everything the Trumps had released from the event, held on a pair of private islands. On social media and in the pages of tabloids such as Page Six and Hello! magazine, official photos from the weekend showed an intimate chapel ceremony alongside lavish beach parties. Several photos depicted guests, including Jared Kushner and Eric Trump, and we scanned them all for signs of Kremlev. Still, nothing had turned up yet.

We then turned to Kremlev’s social media profiles on the off chance that he’d posted about the wedding. Incredibly, on Telegram, Kremlev had posted videos over the same weekend as Trump Jr.’s wedding that appeared to be from someplace tropical. In one, a single detail caught our attention: As Kremlev speaks in Russian to the camera, the frame gives a partial view of an outdoor patio setting. It wasn’t palm trees or crystal water we noticed, but the wicker furniture.

title: ‘A place of silence, contemplation, and beauty can also become a form of resistance,’ in conversation with Catalan artist Jaume Amigó
content:
‘[P]ainters cannot escape the state the world is currently in. In my work, I try to seek out another reality …’

Originally published on Global Voices

Jaume Amigó, ‘Papers d’aigua I,’ 2023. Acrylic on paper, 290 x 420 cm (114.2 × 165.4 in). Photo courtesy of the artist.

For Jaume Amigó, painting can be a form of resistance, not by reproducing the violence and disorder of the present, but by creating an alternative space within it. At a moment saturated with immediate and often brutal images, the Catalan artist turns toward silence, contemplation, beauty and the rhythms of nature. “Painting is also a way of taking a position,” he says, through “the creation of another possible space” that, by contrast, “can also become a form of resistance.”

Born in Barcelona in 1963, Amigó studied engraving and printmaking at the Llotja School of Art and Design. Painting remains central to his practice, but he has also worked in sculpture, ceramics, engraving, installation and scenography. Based in l’Alzina de Ribelles, in Catalonia’s La Noguera region, he has exhibited widely in Spain and abroad, including in Japan, Morocco, the Netherlands and Switzerland.

title: Statement: AlgorithmWatch im Innenausschuss zu KI-basierter Überwachung: Biometrische Massenerkennungssysteme müssen verboten werden!
content:
Berlin, 18. September 2026 – Am Montag, den 21. September 2026, behandelt der Innenausschuss des Deutschen Bundestags die Gesetzentwürfe zur Massenüberwachung mittels Biometrie und KI-Systemen für das Bundeskriminalamt, die Bundespolizei und das Bundesamt für Migration und Flüchtlinge, die das Bundesministerium des Innern (BMI) und das Bundesministerium der Justiz und für Verbraucherschutz (BMJV) vorgelegt haben. Pia Sombetzki, Senior Policy Managerin bei AlgorithmWatch, wurde von der Linksfraktion als Sachverständige eingeladen und wird in ihrer Stellungnahme erneut die Gesetzeswidrigkeit der vorgeschlagenen Maßnahmen betonen und die vollständige Rücknahme der Entwürfe sowie ein grundsätzliches gesetzliches Verbot des Einsatzes biometrischer Massenerkennungssysteme für öffentliche und private Stellen fordern.

Damit unterstreicht AlgorithmWatch die bereits vielfach geäußerte Kritik an den Gesetzen: Die vorgeschlagenen Befugnisse sind europarechtswidrig, verletzen verfassungsrechtliche Mindestanforderungen und widersprechen datenschutzrechtlichen Grundsätzen.

Pia Sombetzki hebt hervor: „Die Bundesregierung schafft mit den Gesetzen nichts anderes als die technische Voraussetzung für eine flächendeckende Verfolgung aller Menschen im öffentlichen Raum. Im Internet öffentlich zugängliche Daten können so gut wie alles umfassen, sowohl das Foto von der letzten Demonstration als auch das Urlaubsvideo mit den Kindern. All diese Daten zu erfassen, ist weder erforderlich für die Arbeit von Ermittlungs- und Strafverfolgungsbehörden noch verhältnismäßig. Allerdings hat es eine zutiefst einschüchternde Wirkung: Menschen wissen zukünftig nicht, ob, wann und wie Foto-, Video- oder Tonaufnahmen von ihnen durch KI-Systeme von Polizei- oder Migrationsbehörden ausgewertet werden.

title: Russia’s Rigged Elections Still Serve a Purpose
content:
The outcome of Russia’s parliamentary elections is predetermined. Yet the Kremlin cares about much more than the figures announced once the ballots are (mis)counted.

Vladimir Putin’s regime can of course falsify almost any result. Independent election monitoring has been largely destroyed, voting has been extended over three days, and electronic ballots are difficult to verify. But an entirely fictional election would cease to perform its most important function. It would tell the Kremlin nothing about the discipline of its officials, the resilience of regional elites, or the state’s ability to mobilize the population.

Russian elections are therefore more than a falsified vote count. They are a nationwide examination of the Putin system. Citizens play a secondary role. The real examinees are governors, bureaucrats, directors of state institutions, and party functionaries.

From September 18 to 20, Russians elect a new State Duma. At the same time, more than 2,200 regional and municipal elections will take place across the country, distributing approximately 20,700 elected offices and legislative seats.

title: "We Are the 99%": 15 Years Later, Occupy Wall Street's Impact Is Still Being Felt
content:
Fifteen years ago this week, thousands of activists marched on the Financial District in New York City. They formed the Occupy Wall Street encampment in Zuccotti Park, launching a movement focused on economic inequality that spread across the nation and globe under the slogan, “We are the 99%.” Protesters would go on to sleep in Zuccotti Park for nearly two months before police raided the encampment.

“Occupy Wall Street changed the public’s common sense about class and class struggle and inequality in this country,” says Yotam Marom, who helped organize the Occupy protests in New York City. “It’s hard to see how you get a Bernie Sanders 2016 run without the public shifting its relationship to that story.”

Marom says Occupy participants were inspired by mass protests happening around the world at that time, including the Arab Spring and the anti-austerity movement in Spain known as the Indignados.

Still, “We got it wrong on a lot of things. We had a ton of internal conflict that really jeopardized the project,” he says.

Marom’s new book is For Louder Days: Reaching Beyond a Politics of Powerlessness.

title: What does a stronger Europe actually require? Demos Helsinki’s comments on the State of the Union.
content:
President von der Leyen highlighted in her State of the Union speech on 16 September a Europe that must become more capable of acting on its own terms: stronger in defence, more secure in energy, more competitive in technology, and more resilient in the face of climate and social pressures.

However, strengthening Europe is not only a question of ambition. It raises difficult questions about dependencies, governance and what we actually mean by resilience. Drawing on research from three EU-funded projects, we look at some of the tensions behind the speech: what technological sovereignty requires in practice, how climate resilience depends on institutions that can work across policy silos, and why Europe’s strength cannot be measured solely through current economic indicators.

title: How Poland “planned to occupy Czech lands” – coordinated information operation exposed
content:
Facebook posts called on people to gather for a protest in the Czech border town of Třinec on Saturday, 29th of August. The protest never took place. The Třinec municipal authorities had already announced that no public event had been registered, while the Czech Republic’s largest trade union, KOVO, which represents metalworking and industrial workers and whose logo was used in the protest advertising materials, denied any connection with the action. Moreover, Polish and Czech media had already exposed the disinformation campaign, which involved fake social media profiles, fabricated media outlets, forged documents and even an unauthorised publication of an article on the website of a public broadcaster.

At the beginning of August, disinformation began circulating claiming that Poland planned to take over more than 600 hectares of Czech territory. According to an analysis by the Czech news portal Seznam Zprávy, several social media accounts in the Czech Republic circulated a document purportedly sent by the Polish government to the Czech authorities. It allegedly demanded that land with a total area of 638.44 hectares be handed over to Poland.

title: EFF Statement on California Governor's Executive Order on AI
content:
California Gov. Gavin Newsom's executive order is an opportunity for a needed, thoughtful conversation about artificial intelligence and its potential harms. Everyday Californians are feeling real anxiety about the risks of artificial intelligence, and as an organization that works to ensure technology empowers people, EFF welcomes this order as a way for the state of California to lead a much-needed dialogue that addresses these concerns. 

Nonetheless, the most immediate and current concerns with this technology are not about sci-fi scenarios concerning rogue super-intelligence. They are happening right now through biased algorithmic decision-making for employment or government benefits, AI-powered surveillance systems such as Flock cameras, and artificially inflated personalized pricing. People want state and federal leaders to act, and we urge Gov. Newsom to develop thoughtful policies to address those concerns. Today’s EO is a good start.

The acclaimed British-Turkish author Elif Shafak is the winner of the Helena Vaz da Silva European Award for Raising Public Awareness on Cultural Heritage 2026. title: Moscow cries fraud abroad while fixing the vote at home
content:
Moscow routinely portrays elections in democratic countries as fraudulent and controlled from abroad. Yet Russia’s own parliamentary election offers no genuine political choice: the Kremlin controls the field and has eliminated even the possibility of voting against the war in Ukraine. As the war’s effects reach deeper into everyday life, growing public dissatisfaction is being kept out of the ballot box.

When post-Soviet states turn away from Russia, as Armenia or Moldova have done, Kremlin officials and aligned outlets usually blame Western interference. Yet Moscow has itself tries to influence elections through foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI), often alongside financial support for pro-Russian groups. Moldovan authorities say Russian agents spent about €200 million – nearly 1% of Moldova’s GDP – on vote-buying and disinformation during the country’s 2024 presidential election and EU referendum. Investigators later found that the sanctioned Russian organisation Evrazia had used similar tactics ahead of Armenia’s 2026 election. Moscow nevertheless portrayed EU assistance intended to counter such threats as election interference.

title: Samtal om Själö hospital – kvinnoöden på 1800-talet
content:
Tidpunkt: 26.10 klockan 18.00-19.00
Plats: Finlandsinstitutet
Adress: Snickarbacken 4, Stockholm
Språk: svenska
Inträde: Gratis, men anmäl dig gärna här gärna här

Berättelsen om Själös kvinnoöden fortsätter att fascinera den finländska befolkningen och är igen aktuell i och med den nya finländska långfilmen Berätta för alla. På Själö, en ö i Åbolands skärgård, har ett av Finlands äldsta sjukhus fungerat i över 350 år. Men det var på 1800-talet som sjukhuset mer eller mindre förvandlades till ett sjukhus för enbart kvinnor. Kvinnor som beskrevs som obotligt sjuka men som i hög grad bestod av individer som samhället helt enkelt inte ville veta av. Och de allra flesta kvinnor som kom till Själö blev kvar resten av livet.

I samband med premiären av Berätta för alla ordnar vi ett samtal om Själös kvinnoöden och kanske ställer vi oss frågan, hade också jag hamnat där? För hur ser den samhälleliga blicken på kvinnor egentligen ut idag och vad är det med Själö som fortsätter att beröra?

I samtalet deltar bland annat författaren Johanna Holmström som skrivit boken Själarnas ö och skådespelaren Marketta Tikkanen från den högaktuella filmen Berätta för alla.
